1	# muneem — Design Document
2	
3	> Status: **draft, pre-implementation**. This document captures the vision, the pipeline shape, the security posture, and the open decisions to resolve before code lands. It is intentionally opinionated where the author has a strong view, and explicitly undecided where the trade-offs need a human call.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. What muneem is
8	
9	**muneem** is a personal-finance bookkeeper that ingests financial documents from the user's email accounts, unlocks the password-protected ones, parses them into a normalized schema, stores them in a local database, and surfaces analytics across the user's full financial life.
10	
11	The name is the Hindi word for the traditional household/business bookkeeper — a trusted figure who maintained the family ledger by hand. This project is the same role, automated.
12	
13	**Single user. Local-first. Privacy-critical.**
14	
15	## 2. Why
16	
17	The user's financial life today is fragmented across many silos:
18	
19	- 3–5 bank accounts (statements arrive monthly as password-protected PDFs)
20	- Multiple credit cards (monthly bills, also password-protected PDFs)
21	- Brokerage and mutual-fund accounts (quarterly statements, portfolio snapshots)
22	- Grocery and shopping receipts (Swiggy, Zomato, Amazon, Flipkart, BigBasket, Blinkit — mostly plain HTML/PDF in email body)
23	- Utility bills, insurance premiums, EMI schedules
24	- Promotional offers and coupons (often forgotten)
25	
26	Each silo has its own portal, login, and format. There is no consolidated view. **The inbox is the only place where they already converge.**
27	
28	Concrete use-cases the user wants once this exists:
29	
30	1. **Grocery & shopping price intelligence** — track what was bought, where, and at what price, over time. Detect when a merchant is no longer competitive on staples.
31	2. **Investment portfolio timeline** — a single time-series of holdings across brokers, so allocation drift and rebalancing decisions are obvious.
32	3. **Bank/card comparison** — fees paid, interest earned, reward redemption efficiency, surfaced as objective numbers.
33	4. **Item catalog** — every significant purchase linked to its receipt/invoice, so warranty windows, return windows, and replacement cycles are queryable.
34	5. **Forgotten-deals reminder** — surface the unused coupons and offers already sitting in the inbox (this is the original goal of the predecessor project; see § 11).
35	
36	## 3. Origin
37	
38	muneem is the successor to `~/Projects/Email-Mining`, a small prototype the user built earlier that extracted promo codes from manually-saved email PDFs using PyMuPDF + Gemini for image OCR. Same insight ("the inbox contains structured value I'm forgetting"), generalized scope.
39	
40	See [`docs/prior-art-email-mining.md`](./docs/prior-art-email-mining.md) for what it did, what to inherit, and what not to.
41	
42	## 4. The pipeline (five stages)
43	
44	Each stage is independent enough to develop and test in isolation. They communicate through well-defined data boundaries (raw files on disk → unlocked files on disk → structured records in DB → derived views).
45	
46	### Stage 1 — Email ingestion
47	
48	**Goal:** pull messages and attachments from Gmail and Outlook into a local staging area.
49	
50	- **Gmail:** [Gmail API](https://developers.google.com/gmail/api) over OAuth2. Read-only scope (`gmail.readonly`). Supports server-side search queries (`has:attachment filename:pdf from:hdfc newer_than:90d`) which is far cheaper than pulling everything and filtering locally. Has good rate limits for personal use.
51	- **Outlook:** [Microsoft Graph API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/mail-api-overview) over OAuth2. Read-only scope (`Mail.Read`). Similar search capability.
52	- **Why not IMAP:** worse search, no labels, harder OAuth, and we lose Gmail's powerful query syntax. Use the native APIs.
53	
54	Mechanically straightforward. The main design questions are: **how is "financial document" detected** (sender allowlist? subject patterns? attachment heuristics? hybrid?), and **how is incremental sync state tracked** (Gmail `historyId` / Graph `deltaLink`).
55	
56	### Stage 2 — Attachment unlocking
57	
58	**Goal:** decrypt password-protected PDFs.
59	
60	The decryption itself is trivial — every mainstream PDF library handles the standard security handler. In Go, `github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu`; in Python, `pikepdf` or `pypdf`.
61	
62	The real design question is **where the passwords come from.** Indian bank and CC statement passwords are almost always derived from user attributes:
63	
64	- "First 4 letters of name (uppercase) + DDMM of DOB" — common at HDFC, ICICI
65	- "PAN number" — common at some brokers
66	- "Last 4 digits of card number" — common for CC statements
67	- "Customer ID" — some banks
68	- "Mobile number" — utilities
69	
70	Three plausible approaches, each with trade-offs:
71	
72	| Approach | Pro | Con |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| **Per-sender rule template** the user configures once (e.g., `from:alerts@hdfcbank.net → first4(name)+ddmm(dob)`) | Deterministic, no guessing, auditable | Requires upfront setup; rules must be maintained as banks change formats |
75	| **Candidate dictionary** (try a small list of derived strings per PDF) | Zero config; "just works" | Brute-forceable feel; fails noisily on unknown senders |
76	| **Interactive prompt** (ask the user the first time, cache for that sender) | Safe, simple | Friction during initial backfill of years of statements |
77	
78	A hybrid is likely best: candidate dictionary first, fall back to rule template, fall back to interactive prompt. **Decision parked.** See § 8.
79	
80	### Stage 3 — Document parsing
81	
82	**This is the hard 80% of the project.** Every issuer's PDF layout is different and changes over time.
83	
84	The space of approaches, in increasing robustness and cost:
85	
86	1. **Per-issuer regex/template parsers.** Precise; brittle. One parser per format, breaks when the issuer redesigns. Realistic for the top ~5 senders that dominate volume.
87	2. **Text-layer extraction + structural heuristics.** Pull text with `pdfcpu` / `pdfplumber` / PyMuPDF; rely on coordinates and font runs to recover tables. Works well for "born digital" PDFs (most bank statements); fails on scanned/image PDFs.
88	3. **OCR (Tesseract) for image-based PDFs and embedded raster content.** Slower; need layout reconstruction.
89	4. **LLM-assisted structured extraction.** Hand page text (+ optionally page rasters) to a model with a target JSON schema. Generalizes across layouts; expensive per page; **must be local for sensitive document categories**. Options: Ollama-hosted models (Llama 3, Qwen, Mistral), or a small purpose-built model.
90	
91	In practice this will be **a hybrid**: deterministic template parsers for the top ~5 high-volume senders (where they pay for themselves), LLM-assisted extraction as the long-tail fallback. Promo emails and other non-sensitive categories can use cloud LLMs; bank/card/investment statements **must not** without explicit per-category approval.
92	
93	Embedded image deduplication (Email-Mining used MD5 hash + SSIM) is a real win here: bank statements repeat the same logo/letterhead on every page, and we don't want to OCR that 30 times per document.
94	
95	### Stage 4 — Normalization & storage
96	
97	**Goal:** map heterogeneous parser outputs into one schema, persist locally.
98	
99	Storage: **SQLite**. Single file, no server, easy to back up, easy to encrypt at rest (SQLCipher), good enough performance for years of personal data. The schema needs to span:
100	
101	- `documents` — every ingested file with sender, date, type, hash, path
102	- `accounts` — bank accounts, cards, broker accounts, identified by issuer + last-4 or similar
103	- `transactions` — line items from statements, normalized (date, amount, currency, counterparty, category, source_document)
104	- `holdings` — point-in-time snapshots of investment positions per account
105	- `merchants` — canonicalized merchant identities (so "SWIGGY*BANGALORE", "Swiggy Instamart", and "SWIGGY BNGLR" collapse to one)
106	- `items` — line-items from itemized receipts (grocery, shopping)
107	- `offers` — promotional offers/coupons with expiry, source, redemption status
108	
109	The merchant canonicalization step is non-trivial — it deserves its own thought (fuzzy match + manual override table is the usual answer).
110	
111	### Stage 5 — Analytics & insights
112	
113	**Goal:** turn the normalized DB into the use-cases in § 2.
114	
115	Once the data is in the schema, the analytics are mostly SQL + light application logic. Likely surface: a local CLI initially, possibly a small local web UI later. Notebook-style exploration is fine for prototyping queries before they're promoted to first-class views.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## 5. Security posture (first class)
120	
121	The threat model deserves to be stated plainly: **muneem aggregates the user's entire financial life — every account, every transaction, every holding — into one local store. That store is a honeypot.** A leak would be catastrophic.
122	
123	Standing rules:
124	
125	1. **All raw statement data stays on the local machine.** No cloud sync of the staging dir or the DB.
126	2. **No cloud LLM APIs for sensitive document categories** (bank, CC, broker, MF, insurance) without explicit per-category user approval discussed in the current session. The default extraction path for these is local (Tesseract + local LLM via Ollama, or deterministic parsers).
127	3. **Non-sensitive categories** (promo emails, generic newsletters, public receipts) may use cloud LLMs after a privacy review of the specific content type.
128	4. **DB encrypted at rest** (SQLCipher or equivalent), key never in the repo.
129	5. **OAuth tokens** stored in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain), not on disk.
130	6. **Logs must not contain extracted statement text.** Sanitize aggressively; redact account numbers, balances, line-items.
131	7. **Nothing sensitive ever in git.** `.gitignore` blocks real PDFs, the DB file, `.env`, and password files. Do not weaken it.
132	
133	## 6. Non-goals (for v1)
134	
135	- **Multi-user / SaaS / hosted product.** Single user, single machine.
136	- **Cloud sync of raw data.** Period.
137	- **Cracking unknown passwords.** muneem decrypts PDFs the user is authorized to read, using passwords the user knows or can derive.
138	- **Browser scraping bank portals.** Email APIs only. Portal scraping is a fragile, ToS-fraught rabbit hole; we deliberately avoid it.
139	- **Real-time alerting / push.** Batch-pull on a schedule is sufficient.
140	- **Tax preparation, investment advice, or anything regulated.** muneem surfaces data; the user decides.
141	
142	## 7. Recommended first vertical slice
143	
144	Before generalizing, prove the end-to-end pipeline on the smallest meaningful scope:
145	
146	> **Gmail → one specific bank's monthly statements → unlocked → parsed into `transactions` → stored in SQLite → a CLI command that lists last month's transactions.**
147	
148	This exercises every stage exactly once, on a real input the user cares about, with no detours. It will surface the actual hard parts (which we can only guess at now) and force the open decisions in § 8 to get made on real evidence.
149	
150	Concretely: pick **one** Indian bank statement format the user has many examples of (likely HDFC or ICICI given the user's geography), build the parser for that one format only, and put the rest of the pipeline around it. Then evaluate before generalizing.
151	
152	## 8. Open architectural decisions
153	
154	These are parked for explicit user discussion. **Don't pick silently.**
155	
156	### 8.1 Language
157	
158	| Option | Pro | Con |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| **Go only** | Single binary, easy distribution, great concurrency for the ingestion side, the user already uses Go for the badminton-highlight-indexer project | Weak PDF parsing / OCR / ML ecosystem; rolling our own is painful |
161	| **Python only** | Best-in-class PDF, OCR, and ML libraries (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, Tesseract bindings, Ollama clients, every parser under the sun); fastest to prototype | Heavier deployment story; less ergonomic for the long-running ingestion daemon |
162	| **Go ingestion + Python parsing** | Plays to each language's strengths | Two-language project complexity; inter-process boundary to maintain |
163	
164	Recommended default: **Python-only for v1**, accept the deployment-story cost in exchange for moving fast on the hard parts. Revisit if the ingestion side outgrows Python.
165	
166	### 8.2 Password sourcing strategy
167	
168	See § 4 Stage 2. The hybrid (dictionary → template → prompt) is the natural answer, but the design of the rule-template config format and the candidate dictionary needs a user call.
169	
170	### 8.3 LLM locality, per document category
171	
172	The default is "local for sensitive, cloud allowed for non-sensitive after review." But which models? Ollama with Llama 3 / Qwen / Mistral on the user's hardware? A small fine-tuned model? Cloud (Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini) with strict redaction for the non-sensitive categories?
173	
174	This decision is closely coupled to the user's hardware capacity (GPU? RAM?) and willingness to wait on inference latency.
175	
176	### 8.4 First-slice scope confirmation
177	
178	§ 7 proposes "Gmail + one bank → CLI". Confirm with user before building.
179	
180	### 8.5 Merchant canonicalization approach
181	
182	Fuzzy string matching has well-known failure modes on merchant names. Do we use a curated rules file (user maintains)? A library? A learned model? Defer until real data exposes the actual mess.
183	
184	## 9. Proposed (not built) file layout
185	
186	This is a *suggestion* for once the language decision is made. Don't materialize it prematurely.
187	
188	```
189	muneem/
190	├── README.md
191	├── CLAUDE.md
192	├── DESIGN.md
193	├── docs/
194	│   ├── prior-art-email-mining.md
195	│   └── (future: parser-notes-per-issuer.md, schema.md, threat-model.md)
196	├── testdata/
197	│   ├── promo-emails/         # non-sensitive corpus (in repo)
198	│   └── statements/           # GITIGNORED — real statements, never committed
199	├── (source tree TBD based on § 8.1)
200	└── (DB file, GITIGNORED)
201	```
202	
203	## 10. Glossary
204	
205	- **Muneem** (मुनीम) — traditional Indian household/business bookkeeper.
206	- **Issuer** — the bank, card network, broker, or merchant that produced a document.
207	- **Statement** — a periodic financial summary from an issuer (bank statement, CC bill, broker statement, MF report).
208	- **Holding** — a position in an investment account at a point in time.
209	- **Line item** — a single transaction or itemized purchase row within a statement or receipt.
210	- **Born-digital PDF** — a PDF generated from a software source with a real text layer (most bank statements). Contrast with scanned/image PDFs.
211	
212	## 11. Vision continuity from Email-Mining
213	
214	The predecessor project (`~/Projects/Email-Mining`) extracted promo codes and expiry dates from manually-saved promo email PDFs, using PyMuPDF for text+image extraction and Gemini for image OCR and summarization. Its scope was just "find the coupon I forgot about."
215	
216	muneem **subsumes** that scope. The deals/coupons feature survives as **one of several extraction targets** — one of the analytics surfaces, fed by the same five-stage pipeline that handles bank statements and everything else. The promo-email PDFs from that project are preserved in [`testdata/promo-emails/`](./testdata/promo-emails/) as the first regression corpus.
217	
218	What was learned there and worth keeping: PyMuPDF (fitz) is the right PDF library; image dedup by hash + SSIM is a real win for repeated chrome; the shape "page text + per-image OCR → unified text → structured extraction" generalizes well. What we change: programmatic Gmail/Outlook fetching instead of manual save-as-PDF; local extraction by default for sensitive categories; persistent normalized DB instead of one-shot stdout.
219	
220	Full details in [`docs/prior-art-email-mining.md`](./docs/prior-art-email-mining.md).
221

1	# Prior art: Email-Mining
2	
3	> A short technical and conceptual writeup of the predecessor project at `~/Projects/Email-Mining`, captured here so muneem's contributors don't need to read that repo cold. Last reviewed against the Email-Mining repo at commit `4b347c6` ("Gemini changes"), April 2025.
4	
5	## What it was
6	
7	A small exploration repo from April 2025 with two halves:
8	
9	1. **NLP learning notebooks** (`Tokenization/`, `Text2Vec/`) — standard NLTK tutorial material: tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, NER, stopwords, bag-of-words, SMS spam corpus. Learning artifacts; not relevant to muneem.
10	2. **A PDF extraction prototype** (`textExtract/`) — *this is the actual seed of muneem.* A working end-to-end pipeline that took a manually-saved promotional email (saved as PDF) and returned a short summary highlighting any promo code and expiry date.
11	
12	## Repo layout (relevant parts)
13	
14	```
15	Email-Mining/
16	├── README.md                                  # 5 lines of setup instructions
17	└── textExtract/
18	    ├── ExtractbyURL/
19	    │   └── extract2.py                        # URL → text + dedup'd images (BeautifulSoup + SSIM)
20	    ├── pdfFiles/                              # ~10 saved promo emails as PDFs
21	    │   ├── Category1/                         # 2 PDFs (DataQuest, MakeMyTrip)
22	    │   ├── Category2/                         # 7 PDFs (AirAsia x3, Flipkart, MakeMyTrip, Swiggy, Unacademy)
23	    │   └── TestSet/                           # 1 held-out PDF (TataNeu)
24	    └── pythonFiles/
25	        ├── extract_ImgTxt.py                  # main entry: PDF → text + images → OCR → summarize
26	        ├── imageText.py                       # Gemini Vision API wrapper for image OCR
27	        ├── summarize.py                       # Gemini text API wrapper for promo-code extraction
28	        └── extracted_content/                 # outputs from the last run
29	```
30	
31	## The pipeline (as it existed)
32	
33	```
34	manually saved email-as-PDF
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	PyMuPDF (fitz).open()
38	        │  • per-page get_text("text")  → page text
39	        │  • per-page get_images(full=True)
40	        │     ├─ filter by size (≥ 300×300)
41	        │     └─ dedupe by MD5 hash of PNG bytes
42	        ▼
43	for each surviving image:
44	   Gemini 1.5 Flash with prompt "Extract all the available text from the image."
45	        │
46	        ▼
47	concatenated text  =  page text + "\n--- Text from imageN ---\n" + image OCR text
48	        │
49	        ▼
50	Gemini 1.5 Flash with prompt
51	   "Give me a very short summary of this email text. If some promo code is
52	    available, please include it, and its expiry date. If not available, then
53	    give 1-2 line containing the main words."
54	        │
55	        ▼
56	stdout
57	```
58	
59	Run with: `GEMINI_API_KEY=... python extract_ImgTxt.py` after editing line 55 to point at a PDF.
60	
61	## Why this matters to muneem
62	
63	The vision is the same: **structured value sits in the user's inbox, going unread; extract it.** Email-Mining narrowed that to "promo codes I'm forgetting." muneem widens it to the user's full financial life, with the forgotten-deals use-case surviving as one of several analytics surfaces.
64	
65	This is not a pivot. It is a generalization.
66	
67	## Patterns to carry forward
68	
69	1. **PyMuPDF (`fitz`) for joint text + image extraction.** It's the right library; do the same in muneem.
70	2. **Image deduplication by hash + SSIM.** Bank statements repeat the same letterhead/logo on every page. Without dedup we'd OCR identical chrome 30 times per document. Email-Mining used MD5 of PNG bytes + `skimage.metrics.structural_similarity` with a 0.95 threshold. Reasonable starting point.
71	3. **The pipeline *shape*** — *page text + per-image OCR → unified text → structured extraction*. This generalizes from "free-form summary" to "structured fields per schema" cleanly. Same pipeline, different sink.
72	4. **The `pdfFiles/` corpus.** Real-world promo PDFs from real Indian merchants are valuable test inputs. Copied to muneem at [`testdata/promo-emails/`](../testdata/promo-emails/).
73	
74	## Choices NOT to inherit
75	
76	1. **Manually saving emails as PDF.** The whole point of muneem is to automate this. Use Gmail API / Microsoft Graph instead.
77	2. **Cloud LLM (Gemini) as the default for everything.** Acceptable for promo codes (low sensitivity); unacceptable for bank balances, transaction lines, holdings. See muneem's `DESIGN.md` § 5 (Security posture).
78	3. **One-shot stdout.** Replace with persistent normalized storage (SQLite per `DESIGN.md` § 4 Stage 4).
79	4. **Edit-line-55-to-change-input.** The prototype hardcoded a PDF path inside `extract_ImgTxt.py`. Obvious — make inputs proper arguments / config.
80	5. **No schema, no validation, no error handling.** It's a prototype; muneem isn't.
81	6. **No tests.** muneem should have at minimum a regression test that runs the pipeline against `testdata/promo-emails/` and asserts that known promo codes are recovered.
82	7. **The NLP notebooks.** Tutorial material. Leave them in Email-Mining as personal reference.
83	
84	## What Email-Mining never had to address (but muneem does)
85	
86	- **Email fetching.** OAuth, scopes, search, rate limits, incremental sync.
87	- **Password-protected PDFs.** Decryption is mechanical; password sourcing is the design problem.
88	- **Heterogeneous formats at scale.** Email-Mining handled ~10 promo emails of broadly similar shape. muneem will see dozens of issuer formats that all look different and change yearly.
89	- **Persistence and normalization.** A schema spanning accounts, transactions, holdings, merchants, items, offers — and a canonicalization story for merchant identity.
90	- **Security as a first-class constraint.** Email-Mining was a coupon-finder; the worst-case leak was a expired DataQuest code. muneem aggregates the user's full financial life — the threat model is categorically different.
91	
92	## The corpus, in muneem
93	
94	All 10 PDFs from Email-Mining's `pdfFiles/` are preserved at [`testdata/promo-emails/`](../testdata/promo-emails/). The original `Category1` / `Category2` / `TestSet` directory split was not obviously documented (likely "simple" / "complex" / "held-out"); the categorization is recorded in that directory's `README.md` for whoever wants to re-establish a train/test split.
95

1	# testdata/promo-emails
2	
3	A small regression corpus of **promotional email PDFs** carried over from the predecessor project `~/Projects/Email-Mining`. These are non-sensitive marketing emails (no account numbers, no balances, no PII beyond the recipient's email address), safe to keep in the repo.
4	
5	## Why these are here
6	
7	These are real-world Indian-merchant promo emails saved as PDFs. Each contains some combination of:
8	- promo codes (the original extraction target)
9	- expiry dates
10	- terms & conditions
11	- banner imagery with text rasterized into the image (the reason image-OCR was needed in the predecessor)
12	
13	They serve as the **first regression corpus** for muneem's "forgotten deals" extraction target — the use-case carried forward from Email-Mining. A passing test on this corpus should recover the known promo codes from each PDF.
14	
15	## Contents
16	
17	| Filename | Issuer | Original category | Notes |
18	|---|---|---|---|
19	| `airasia-1.pdf` | AirAsia | Category2 | 3.7 MB — large image content |
20	| `airasia-2.pdf` | AirAsia | Category2 | |
21	| `airasia-3.pdf` | AirAsia | Category2 | |
22	| `dataquest.pdf` | DataQuest | Category1 | Smallest (57 KB) — likely mostly text |
23	| `flipkart.pdf` | Flipkart | Category2 | |
24	| `makemytrip-1.pdf` | MakeMyTrip | Category2 | |
25	| `makemytrip-2.pdf` | MakeMyTrip | Category1 | 3.8 MB — heavy banner imagery |
26	| `swiggy.pdf` | Swiggy | Category2 | |
27	| `tataneu.pdf` | TataNeu | TestSet | 13.9 MB — largest; was held out in predecessor |
28	| `unacademy.pdf` | Unacademy | Category2 | |
29	
30	The original `Category1` / `Category2` / `TestSet` split in Email-Mining was not explicitly documented but appears to have been a rough "simple / complex / held-out" partition. Preserved here in the table above in case anyone wants to re-establish a train/test split.

33	
34	Carried forward verbatim from `Projects/Email-Mining/textExtract/pdfFiles/{Category1,Category2,TestSet}/`. Only the filenames were normalized (lowercased, kebab-cased).

1	# muneem
2	
3	**Your automated muneem — a personal-finance bookkeeper that pulls financial documents from your inbox, unlocks them, and builds a local consolidated ledger.**
4	
5	In traditional Indian households a *muneem* (मुनीम) was the trusted bookkeeper who tracked every statement, bill, and transaction on the family's behalf. This project is the same idea, automated and personal.
6	
7	## What it does (intended)
8	
9	Reads Gmail and Outlook for financial documents (bank statements, credit-card bills, brokerage statements, mutual-fund reports, utility bills, grocery and shopping receipts), decrypts the password-protected ones, parses them into a normalized local database, and surfaces insights:
10	
11	- Grocery/shopping price-tracking across merchants over time
12	- Investment portfolio timeline and cross-broker view
13	- Bank/card performance comparison
14	- Catalog of purchased items with their bills (warranty, returns, age)
15	- Forgotten deals and coupons sitting unread in your inbox
16	
17	## Status
18	
19	**Greenfield.** This repo currently contains design docs, a small test corpus, and prior-art notes. No application code yet. See [`DESIGN.md`](./DESIGN.md) for the plan and [`docs/prior-art-email-mining.md`](./docs/prior-art-email-mining.md) for what came before.
20	
21	## Privacy
22	
23	Single-user, fully local by design. All raw statement data stays on the machine. See `DESIGN.md` § Security for the threat model and standing rules.
24

16	def extract_text_and_images_from_pdf(pdf_path, save_dir='extracted_content'):
17	    text = ""
18	    images = []
19	    minWidth = 300
20	    minHeight = 300
21	    seen_hashes = set()
22	
23	    # Create directory to save images if it doesn't exist
24	    if not os.path.exists(save_dir):
25	        os.makedirs(save_dir)
26	
27	    pdf_document = fitz.open(pdf_path)
28	    for page_num in range(len(pdf_document)):
29	        page = pdf_document.load_page(page_num)
30	        text += page.get_text("text")
31	
32	        image_list = page.get_images(full=True)
33	        for img_index, img in enumerate(image_list):
34	            xref = img[0]
35	            base_image = pdf_document.extract_image(xref)
36	            image_bytes = base_image["image"]
37	            image_ext = base_image["ext"]
38	            image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(image_bytes))
39	
40	            # Save required image with sequential name
41	            width, height = img[2], img[3]
42	            if width >= minWidth and height >= minHeight:
43	                image_hash = compute_image_hash(image)
44	                if image_hash not in seen_hashes:
45	                    seen_hashes.add(image_hash)
46	                    images.append(image)
47	                    image_filename = os.path.join(save_dir, f"image{len(images)}.{image_ext}")
48	                    image.save(image_filename)
49	
50	
51	
52	    return text, images

17	    """Compare two images using Structural Similarity Index."""

19	    img1_gray = np.array(img1.convert('L'))
20	    img2_gray = np.array(img2_resized.convert('L'))
21	    score, _ = ssim(img1_gray, img2_gray, full=True)
22	    return score > 0.95

The organizing idea: **build the architecture on safe, committed data first; attach the sensitive ingestion second.** That inverts the friction curve and keeps the riskiest stages (OAuth, secrets, password sourcing, the hard parser) from all landing at once.

| # | Milestone | What it proves | Touches sensitive data? |

| **3** | **Unlocking (Stage 2)** — PDF decryption + password sourcing per chosen strategy; cache per sender; secrets never in repo/logs | Locked → unlocked; `documents.status` advances | Yes |

DESIGN.md § 7 makes the **bank vertical slice** the first build. I'd instead make the **promo-corpus skeleton (Milestone 1)** come first, then the bank slice. # muneem — Project Plan & Roadmap

> Status: **active plan, pre-implementation.** This is the "how and in what order" companion to [`DESIGN.md`](../DESIGN.md) (the "what and why"). DESIGN.md owns the architecture and the threat model; this doc owns sequencing, milestones, and concrete tasks. Where they disagree, DESIGN.md wins and this doc should be corrected.
>
> Created 2026-05-30.

---

## 1. Decisions locked (2026-05-30)

These resolve open decisions from DESIGN.md § 8. They were made by the user explicitly; this section is the start of the decision log.

| DESIGN.md ref | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| § 8.1 Language | Implementation language for v1 | **Python-only.** Accept the heavier deployment story in exchange for the best PDF/OCR/LLM ecosystem and fastest path on the hard parsing work. Revisit only if the ingestion daemon outgrows Python. |
| § 8.4 First slice | What to build first | **Both tracks in parallel** — the promo-corpus parse→store→query spine *and* the Gmail ingestion plumbing, developed as two decoupled tracks that converge at the first bank slice. |
| § 8.2 Passwords | Password sourcing strategy | **Hybrid: candidate dictionary → per-sender rule template → interactive prompt.** Cache the winning method per sender. Secrets never touch the repo or logs. |
| (practical) | First real bank parser target | **HDFC** — born-digital statements, name+DDMM-style PDF password (per CLAUDE.md), and the issuer with the longest consistent statement history to test against. |

**Still parked** (do not pick silently — see § 9 below): § 8.3 LLM model for *sensitive* categories, § 8.5 merchant canonicalization, and the timing of encryption-at-rest (SQLCipher).

---

## 2. Guiding principles (inherited from DESIGN.md § 5 + CLAUDE.md)

1. **Local by default.** All raw statement data and the DB stay on the machine. OCR/LLM work runs locally for any sensitive category. No cloud sync of staging or DB, ever.
2. **No cloud LLM on sensitive contents** (bank, CC, broker, MF, insurance) without explicit per-category approval in-session. The **promo corpus is the one non-sensitive playground** where cloud LLMs are policy-permitted — so it's where we validate any LLM-extraction pattern *before* it could ever see a statement.
3. **Test on safe, committed data wherever possible.** `testdata/promo-emails/` is the regression corpus and runs in CI. Statement parsing gets CI coverage via **synthetic/redacted fixtures** in the issuer's layout — never real statements.
4. **Secrets discipline.** OAuth tokens → OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager). Nothing sensitive in git; don't weaken `.gitignore`. Logs are redacted (no account numbers, balances, line items, or statement text).
5. **Decisions parked for humans stay parked.** Don't write code that silently locks in § 9's open items.

---

## 3. Proposed Python stack

User-locked is Python-only. The libraries below are *recommendations* (well-known OSS, per CLAUDE.md's "batteries-included stdlib + well-known OSS over novel dependencies") — open to override, not parked decisions. Anything that is a cloud **service** is flagged and needs a nod before adoption.

| Concern | Proposed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Packaging / deps / venv | **uv** + `pyproject.toml` | Fast, modern. Poetry is an equally fine fallback. |
| Lint + format | **ruff** | One tool, fast. |
| Tests | **pytest** | Regression suite runs offline in CI on the promo corpus + synthetic fixtures. |
| PDF text + image extraction | **PyMuPDF (`fitz`)** | Carried from Email-Mining; confirmed the right library. |
| Table recovery (born-digital statements) | **pdfplumber** | Coordinate/word-level extraction for HDFC's transaction tables. |
| PDF decryption | **pikepdf** (libqpdf) | Robust standard-security-handler support. `pypdf` is the fallback. |
| Image dedup | **Pillow + scikit-image SSIM** | Carried from Email-Mining (MD5 hash + SSIM ≥ 0.95). |
| OCR (image PDFs, later) | **Tesseract** via `pytesseract` | Local. Windows needs the Tesseract binary installed (setup task). |
| Gmail | **google-api-python-client + google-auth-oauthlib** | Read-only scope `gmail.readonly`. |
| Secret storage | **keyring** | Uses Windows Credential Manager on win32. |
| DB | **sqlite3 (stdlib)** + lightweight versioned migrations | Encryption-at-rest (SQLCipher via `sqlcipher3`) deferred to Milestone D per DESIGN.md. |
| CLI | **Typer** | Clean ergonomics; `argparse` (stdlib) is the zero-dependency fallback. |
| LLM (promo only, non-sensitive) | deterministic-first; cloud LLM **only if needed and approved** | See § 5 Track A. Sensitive-doc LLM is parked (§ 9 / DESIGN § 8.3). |

---

## 4. Build order at a glance

```
Milestone 0 — Decisions & scaffolding  (no sensitive data)
        │
        ├──────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                               ▼                               
  TRACK A: Promo spine            TRACK B: Gmail ingestion         (run in parallel,
  parse → store → query           fetch → stage → catalog          fully decoupled)
  (committed corpus, CI)          (real email, local only)
        │                               │
        └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                        ▼
        Milestone C — HDFC vertical slice  (CONVERGENCE)
        unlock (hybrid passwords) → HDFC parser → transactions → CLI
        ▷ completes DESIGN.md § 7
                        │
                        ▼
        Milestone D — Harden & evaluate  (the pre-generalize checkpoint)
                        │
                        ▼
        Generalize  (more issuers, local-LLM fallback, holdings, items, analytics, UI)
```

Tracks A and B are genuinely independent: A needs no OAuth and no secrets; B needs no parsing. As a single developer you can interleave them in any order — neither blocks the other. **Both must land before Milestone C**, where a fetched-and-unlocked HDFC PDF flows through the parser for the first time.

Effort tags below are rough (S / M / L), for relative sequencing only — not calendar estimates.

---

## 5. Milestones & tasks

### Milestone 0 — Decisions & scaffolding · no sensitive data

- [ ] **0.1 (S)** Project skeleton: `pyproject.toml` (uv), package dir (name TBD, e.g. `muneem/`), `ruff` + `pytest` configured. *Do not over-materialize the source tree (DESIGN § 9) — create only what 0.x needs.*
- [ ] **0.2 (S)** Offline CI: GitHub Actions (or local pre-commit) that installs deps and runs `pytest` against committed data only. A trivial `test_smoke` proves the loop is green.
- [ ] **0.3 (S)** Config + secrets foundation: a config loader (env + a gitignored `config.toml`), and a `keyring`-backed secret accessor stub. Confirm `.gitignore` covers `config.toml` and any new secret paths.
- [ ] **0.4 (S)** `gitignore` audit: verify the proposed local-only dirs (`testdata/statements/`, staging dir, `*.db`) are blocked. Add a `testdata/statements/.gitkeep`-style note or README so the expected-but-absent dir is documented.
- **Exit:** `uv run pytest` is green in CI on a clean checkout; repo layout agreed.

### Track A — Promo spine: parse → store → query · committed corpus, fully CI-testable

> Resurrects the Email-Mining deals feature as muneem's first working output. Zero secrets, zero OAuth.

- [ ] **A.1 (M)** Port Email-Mining's extraction into a real module: PyMuPDF per-page `get_text` + `get_images`, size filter (≥300×300), MD5 + SSIM dedup. Replace the edit-line-55 hardcoded path with proper arguments/config. Replace one-shot stdout with a return value.
- [ ] **A.2 (S)** Minimal schema slice + migration v1: `documents` (id, source, external_id, sender, subject, received_date, doc_type, sha256, path, status, created_at) and `offers` (id, document_id, merchant, promo_code, description, expiry_date, redeemed, source_text). Full schema is future work (`docs/schema.md`).
- [ ] **A.3 (M)** Promo extraction, **deterministic-first**: regex/heuristics for promo codes + expiry dates over the unified text. Where deterministic extraction misses, an **LLM fallback** is permitted *because promo is non-sensitive* — but that pulls in a cloud service, so it's gated on a quick okay (reuse Email-Mining's Gemini path, go local via Ollama, or use Anthropic — your call when we get there).
- [ ] **A.4 (M)** `muneem ingest <pdf>` writes a `documents` + `offers` row; `muneem offers list` reads them back. **Ground-truth + regression test:** establish the known promo codes for each of the 10 corpus PDFs, then a `pytest` that runs the pipeline over `testdata/promo-emails/` and asserts recovery. (Building the ground-truth answer key is itself part of this task.)
- **Exit:** `ingest → SQLite → offers list` works end-to-end; green regression test on the committed corpus. Stages 3→4→5 proven with zero risk.

### Track B — Gmail ingestion: fetch → stage → catalog · real email, local only

> First contact with real (sensitive) email. Everything it writes is gitignored.

- [ ] **B.1 (M)** Gmail OAuth2: register a Google Cloud project, `gmail.readonly` scope, store the token in `keyring`. Document the one-time consent flow.
- [ ] **B.2 (M)** Financial-document detection v1: a **sender allowlist** + server-side query (`has:attachment filename:pdf from:… newer_than:…`). Start narrow and precise; broaden later. Pull matching messages + PDF attachments into a gitignored staging dir.
- [ ] **B.3 (S)** Incremental sync: persist Gmail `historyId`; on re-run, fetch only what's new. Idempotent (re-running never duplicates `documents`, keyed by message id + attachment hash).
- [ ] **B.4 (S)** Catalog fetched attachments as `documents` rows (status `locked`/`unparsed`), with sha256 + staging path. `muneem fetch --since 90d` is the entry point.
- **Exit:** `muneem fetch` populates the staging dir + `documents` rows from a narrow real-Gmail query. (Manual/local verification — not CI; it touches a real account.)

### Milestone C — HDFC vertical slice · CONVERGENCE · completes DESIGN.md § 7

> A fetched HDFC statement gets unlocked and parsed into real transactions. This is the moment every stage runs once on real data the user cares about.

- [ ] **C.1 (M)** Unlocking (Stage 2) with the **hybrid** strategy: candidate dictionary derived from user attributes (e.g. `first4(name).upper() + DDMM(dob)`) → per-sender rule template → interactive prompt. Cache the winning method per sender in the keychain. **No password material in repo or logs.** Decrypt with pikepdf; advance `documents.status` to `unlocked`.
- [ ] **C.2 (L)** HDFC parser (Stage 3, the hard 80%): born-digital text-layer + pdfplumber table recovery → normalized transactions (txn_date, value_date, amount, direction, narration, running balance). **Synthetic HDFC-layout fixtures** committed for CI; real statements stay gitignored locally.
- [ ] **C.3 (M)** Schema migration v2: `accounts` (issuer, account_type, last4, holder) + `transactions` (account_id, document_id, txn fields, category, merchant_id-nullable). Populate from the parser. `muneem txns list --last-month` prints real parsed transactions.
- **Exit:** **DESIGN.md § 7 vertical slice complete** — Gmail → HDFC statement → unlocked → parsed → SQLite → CLI lists last month's transactions, on real data, locally.

### Milestone D — Harden & evaluate · the pre-generalize checkpoint

- [ ] **D.1 (M)** Redacted structured logging (assert no statement text / account numbers leak); idempotent, resumable re-runs across all stages.
- [ ] **D.2 (S)** Encryption-at-rest decision (DESIGN § 5.4): adopt SQLCipher now or schedule it. (Parked item — bring evidence, then decide.)
- [ ] **D.3 (M)** **Evaluation writeup:** how well did the deterministic HDFC parser hold across statement vintages? Where does it break? Which categories will need the local-LLM fallback? This is the evidence DESIGN § 7 asks for *before* generalizing. Capture in `docs/parser-notes-hdfc.md`.
- **Exit:** the slice is robust and re-runnable; a written go/no-go on generalization with real evidence.

---

## 6. Generalize (post-checkpoint backlog — scope after Milestone D)

Ordered roughly by leverage, not committed:

- Second/third bank parsers + the first **credit-card bill** parser (reuses unlock + parser scaffolding).
- **Local-LLM long-tail fallback** (Ollama) for issuers that don't justify a bespoke parser — **local, because these are sensitive** (resolves DESIGN § 8.3).
- Broker / MF statements → `holdings` (point-in-time positions; the investment-timeline use-case).
- Itemized receipts (Swiggy/Amazon/BigBasket/etc.) → `items` (the price-intelligence + catalog use-cases).
- **Merchant canonicalization** → `merchants` (DESIGN § 8.5 — defer until real data exposes the actual mess, then decide rules-file vs. library vs. learned).
- Analytics surfaces for the DESIGN § 2 use-cases (CLI views first; optional small **local** web UI later).

---

## 7. Cross-cutting workstreams (run throughout, not a phase)

- **Security & secrets hygiene** — keychain for tokens + cached passwords; redacted logs; gitignore audits each milestone; encryption-at-rest tracked to D.2.
- **Schema migrations from day one** — versioned migration scripts; the schema *will* churn as new issuers land. Keep `docs/schema.md` current.
- **Test-corpus curation** — ground-truth answer key for the promo corpus (A.4); synthetic/redacted statement fixtures for CI (C.2). Never commit real statements.
- **Decision log** — append resolutions to § 1 here and mark the corresponding DESIGN.md § 8 item resolved.

---

## 8. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Sensitive data leaks into git, logs, or a cloud LLM | Local-by-default; promo-only LLM playground; redacted logging (D.1); gitignore audits; the § 2 principles are non-negotiable. |
| HDFC parser is brittle across statement vintages | Synthetic fixtures + the D.3 evaluation gate *before* generalizing; deterministic-first with a planned local-LLM fallback for the long tail. |
| Password sourcing fails noisily on backfill | Hybrid strategy degrades to interactive prompt; cache per sender so it's a one-time cost. |
| Gmail OAuth / quota friction | Read-only scope, server-side queries (cheap), incremental `historyId` sync; narrow allowlist first. |
| Scope creep into the full § 2 vision before the slice works | Hard checkpoint at Milestone D; generalization is explicitly post-checkpoint. |
| Two parallel tracks diverge / integration surprises at C | Both write through the *same* `documents` table and schema-migration discipline from A.2/B.4, so convergence is a join, not a rewrite. |

---

## 9. Still-open decisions (do NOT pick silently)

Carried from DESIGN.md § 8, not yet resolved — surface and ask when a milestone forces them:

- **§ 8.3 — LLM model for sensitive categories.** Coupled to your hardware (GPU? RAM?) and latency tolerance. Forced at the start of the generalize phase (local-LLM fallback). Ollama + Llama/Qwen/Mistral is the likely shape, but unconfirmed.
- **§ 8.5 — Merchant canonicalization.** Deferred until real receipt data exposes the mess. Forced when `items`/`merchants` land.
- **Encryption-at-rest timing** (D.2) — SQLCipher now vs. later.
- **Promo-track LLM** (A.3) — only reached if deterministic extraction underperforms; cloud is policy-permitted for promo but still needs a quick okay on which vendor.

---

## 10. Definition of done for v1

The DESIGN.md § 7 slice, hardened: **`muneem fetch` pulls HDFC statements from Gmail → unlocks them with the hybrid password strategy → the HDFC parser writes normalized `transactions` to SQLite → `muneem txns list` shows last month's activity — all locally, with redacted logs, idempotent re-runs, green CI on synthetic fixtures, and a written evaluation of where to go next.** The promo "forgotten deals" feature ships alongside as the Track A deliverable.

import fitz, re, os, glob

d = r"C:\Users\avidu\Projects\muneem\testdata\promo-emails"
KEYS = re.compile(r'code|coupon|off|use|%|expir|valid|hurry|save|flat|upto|up to|ends|last', re.I)

for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.pdf"))):
    doc = fitz.open(p)
    text = ""
    big_imgs = 0
    for page in doc:
        text += page.get_text("text")
        for img in page.get_images(full=True):
            w, h = img[2], img[3]
            if w >= 300 and h >= 300:
                big_imgs += 1
    name = os.path.basename(p)
    print(f"=== {name} | pages={doc.page_count} | textchars={len(text)} | bigimgs={big_imgs}")
    seen = set()
    for line in text.splitlines():
        l = line.strip()
        if l and KEYS.search(l) and l not in seen:
            seen.add(l)
            print("   >", l[:130])
    doc.close()
print("PROBE_DONE")

### 44. assistant (2026-05-30T17:20:18.576Z)

# muneem — Testing Strategy

> Status: **active.** Companion to [`ROADMAP.md`](./ROADMAP.md) (sequencing) and [`../DESIGN.md`](../DESIGN.md) (architecture + threat model). This doc owns *how we know muneem works* — and, just as importantly, *how we know it isn't leaking or hallucinating*.
>
> Created 2026-05-30. Grounded in a direct inspection of the committed promo corpus (`testdata/promo-emails/`), not in the abstract.

---

## 1. Principles

1. **Grounded, not aspirational.** Every test tier below maps to a failure mode actually observed in the real corpus (§ 2), not a hypothetical one.
2. **Precision ranks with recall.** A bookkeeper that invents a promo code or a transaction is worse than one that misses it. Negative fixtures (no code present) are first-class.
3. **Test on safe data by default.** The committed promo corpus is non-sensitive and drives CI. Sensitive paths (statements) are tested on **synthetic/redacted fixtures** in CI and on **local-only, gitignored** real data behind an opt-in marker — never real statements in CI or the repo.
4. **CI is offline, deterministic, secretless.** No network, no cloud LLM, no OAuth, no keychain in the default CI run. Non-deterministic steps (OCR, LLM) are mocked/cassette-backed by default and exercised live only behind explicit markers.
5. **Security posture is enforced by tests, not just docs.** Redaction, category-gating of cloud LLMs, and "no sensitive paths tracked in git" are assertions that fail the build (§ 9).
6. **Adding a corpus file means adding its answer-key entry.** The corpus and its ground truth move together (§ 4).

---

## 2. What the corpus actually contains (grounded findings)

Direct inspection of all 10 PDFs — PyMuPDF text-layer extraction (`get_text`) + large-image count (`get_images`, ≥300×300 px, matching the Email-Mining dedup filter) + visual rendering of a sample. This is the empirical basis for everything below.

| PDF | Issuer (from content) | Pages | Text chars | Big imgs | Promo code | Code location | Expiry / validity | Verified |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| `dataquest.pdf` | Dataquest | 3 | 2526 | 0 | `JS231sz` | **text layer** | "Ends Today" + live countdown (relative to send date 2024-07-29) | ✅ text + visual |
| `makemytrip-2.pdf` | MakeMyTrip | 3 | 925 | 7 | `EARLYBIRDDEAL` | **text layer** | "≥15 days in advance" (conditional, not a date) | ✅ text |
| `swiggy.pdf` | Swiggy × ClearTax | 4 | 774 | 3 | `CTSWIGGYUX` | **image only** (OCR) | "before July 31st" (in image) | ✅ visual |
| `flipkart.pdf` | Flipkart | 2 | 555 | 1 | — none — | n/a | "GOAT SALE, 20–25 Jul" (in image) | ✅ negative |
| `airasia-2.pdf` | AirAsia | 2 | 695 | 1 | TBD | image? | "Flat 50% Off Seats, 25% Off Meals" (subject/text) | ⚠️ unverified |
| `airasia-3.pdf` | AirAsia | 2 | 710 | 1 | TBD | image? | "Final Day! Save 15% Off Flights…" (relative) | ⚠️ unverified |
| `airasia-1.pdf` | **Air India Express** (≠ filename) | 3 | 834 | 4 | TBD | image? | "Special Offers" | ⚠️ unverified |
| `makemytrip-1.pdf` | MakeMyTrip | 2 | 1051 | 2 | TBD | image? | "travel dates & save up…" | ⚠️ unverified |
| `unacademy.pdf` | Unacademy | 2 | 555 | 3 | TBD | image? | "Last few hours left Ayush!" (relative, personalized) | ⚠️ unverified |
| `tataneu.pdf` | Tata Neu | 4 | 1581 | 10 | TBD | image? | — | ⚠️ unverified |

**`Verified`** distinguishes ground truth we have *confirmed* (text layer and/or visual read) from entries still **TBD**. We do **not** invent codes for the unverified rows — establishing them (via OCR + a human glance) is an explicit task in ROADMAP A.4. Attribution discipline (CLAUDE.md): if it isn't verified, it's marked unverified.

### Gotchas the real data exposes (each becomes a test)

- **Ligatures in the text layer.** PyMuPDF returns `Oﬀer` / `Oﬀ` (U+FB00 `ﬀ`), not `Offer`/`Off`. Naïve substring/regex matching for "Off"/"Offer" silently fails. → **NFKC normalization** before matching, with a dedicated unit test (`airasia-2`, `airasia-3`).
- **Codes live in images about half the time.** 6 of 10 PDFs carry the offer in rasterized banners (`bigimgs` ≥ 1 and an empty/near-empty text layer). OCR is not optional for the corpus; it is the path for ~half of it.
- **Expiry is rarely a clean date.** Observed forms: absolute-ish ("before July 31st"), relative ("Ends Today", "Final Day!", "Last few hours left"), conditional ("≥15 days in advance"), and a **live countdown timer**. → Expiry parsing must resolve relative phrases against the email's *received date* and tolerate "no hard date."
- **Filename ≠ issuer.** `airasia-1.pdf` is an **Air India Express** mailer. → Issuer detection must derive from sender/content, never the filename. (Also: fix the mislabel in the corpus README.)
- **Third-party PII in fixtures.** Recipient is `Ayush Raina <ayushraina767@gmail.com>` (the prototype's tester, *not* the muneem user), and bodies are personalized ("…left Ayush!"). The corpus README says "no PII beyond the recipient's email address"; in reality the recipient is a *different person* and appears in the body. Treated as **non-sensitive** (promo, already committed, no financial data), but extraction tests must not surface or log it as financial PII, and golden files (§ 5) intentionally retain it as committed non-sensitive content.

---

## 3. Fixture tiers (derived from § 2)

The corpus self-stratifies into capability tiers. Tests are gated by tier so CI stays green and honest about what's proven.

| Tier | Capability under test | Members | CI behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — text-layer codes** | Deterministic extraction, no OCR | `dataquest`, `makemytrip-2` | **Must pass** in default CI (recall + precision = 100%). |
| **T2 — image-only codes** | OCR (Tesseract) → code recovery | `swiggy` (+ any unverified row confirmed image-coded) | Behind `@pytest.mark.ocr`; runs in the optional OCR job, skipped if the Tesseract binary is absent. |
| **T3 — no-code negatives** | Precision / no hallucination | `flipkart` (+ confirmed no-code rows) | **Must pass** in default CI (assert *zero* codes extracted). |
| **T4 — unverified** | Answer key not yet established | the 6 ⚠️ rows | `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False)` until verified in A.4; never block CI on guesses. |

---

## 4. The answer-key file (ground truth)

A single committed file is the source of truth; tests read it, they don't hardcode expectations.

`testdata/promo-emails/expected.yaml` — one entry per PDF:

```yaml
# Seed (created during ROADMAP A.4). verified:false rows are placeholders, NOT assertions.
dataquest.pdf:
  issuer: Dataquest
  codes: ["JS231sz"]
  code_location: text          # text | image | none
  discount: "$706 / lifetime"
  expiry: {type: relative, raw: "Ends Today", resolved_against: received_date}
  verified: true
makemytrip-2.pdf:
  issuer: MakeMyTrip
  codes: ["EARLYBIRDDEAL"]
  code_location: text
  discount: "up to 50% off"
  expiry: {type: conditional, raw: "≥15 days in advance"}
  verified: true
swiggy.pdf:
  issuer: Swiggy            # offer brand: ClearTax
  codes: ["CTSWIGGYUX"]
  code_location: image
  discount: "up to 70% off"
  expiry: {type: absolute, raw: "before July 31st"}
  verified: true
flipkart.pdf:
  issuer: Flipkart
  codes: []                # negative fixture — must extract nothing
  code_location: none
  discount: "GOAT Sale"
  expiry: {type: relative, raw: "20-25 Jul"}
  verified: true
# airasia-1/2/3, makemytrip-1, unacademy, tataneu: verified:false — establish in A.4 (OCR + manual glance).
```

**Process to verify a TBD row (A.4):** run OCR on its large images → propose codes → a human confirms/edits → flip `verified:true`. Until then it stays T4/xfail. New corpus PDF ⇒ new entry, same flow.

---

## 5. Test layers (the pyramid)

**Unit (fast, deterministic, the bulk):**
- PDF text extraction wrapper (pages → text), large-image extraction + size filter.
- **Image dedup**: MD5-of-PNG-bytes equality and SSIM ≥ 0.95 near-duplicate detection (port + test Email-Mining's logic on synthetic image pairs).
- **Text normalization**: NFKC ligature folding (`ﬀ`→`ff`), whitespace, case — table-driven, seeded by § 2 gotchas.
- **Code detection**: regex/heuristics over normalized text; positive cases (`JS231sz`, `EARLYBIRDDEAL`) and adversarial negatives (order numbers, prices like `$706`, dates, the literal word "code" with no token) so precision is pinned.
- **Expiry parsing**: absolute / relative / conditional / none, each resolved against a fixed `received_date`.
- **Schema + migrations**: apply v1→vN on a temp SQLite file; assert idempotent re-apply.

**Component / integration:**
- `ingest(pdf)` end-to-end on a single corpus PDF → assert exact `documents` + `offers` rows (via the answer key), against an in-memory/temp SQLite.

**Regression (corpus):** run the pipeline over `testdata/promo-emails/`, assert per-tier recall/precision from `expected.yaml`. T1+T3 in default CI; T2 in the OCR job; T4 xfail.

**Golden-file (drift detection):** snapshot the unified extracted text per PDF under `testdata/promo-emails/golden/`. A diff flags upstream library/behavior drift. (Non-sensitive promo text only — safe to commit.)

**CLI:** drive `muneem ingest` / `muneem offers list` via subprocess (or the framework's test runner); assert exit codes + stdout shape, not internals.

**Determinism / idempotency:** ingest the same PDF twice → exactly one `documents` row (sha256 dedup), stable output.

---

## 6. Testing the non-deterministic parts (OCR & LLM)

- **OCR (Tesseract, local).** Compare against golden text with a **normalized fuzzy match** (e.g. token-set ratio ≥ threshold), never exact equality. Marker `@pytest.mark.ocr`; auto-skip if the binary is missing so contributors without Tesseract still get a green default suite.
- **LLM extraction (promo only — cloud is policy-permitted for this *non-sensitive* category).**
  - Default CI uses **recorded cassettes** (VCR-style) → deterministic, offline, free.
  - Live calls only behind `@pytest.mark.llm` + an env flag (`MUNEEM_LLM_LIVE=1`); never in default CI.
  - The cassette/fixtures must contain **only** promo-corpus content — enforced by the guard in § 9.

---

## 7. The sensitive path (statements) — coverage without real data in CI

The corpus is promo-only by design. Statement parsing (ROADMAP Milestone C) is tested two ways:

1. **Synthetic fixtures, committed.** A small generator emits fake **HDFC-layout** statement PDFs with faker-generated names/amounts/dates and a *known* derived password. These exercise the parser and the unlocker in CI with zero real data. Stored under `testdata/synthetic/` (committed; clearly fake).
2. **Real statements, local-only.** Behind `@pytest.mark.local_statements`, reading `testdata/statements/` (gitignored). Skipped in CI; run by the user locally.

**Unlocker tests (hybrid strategy, C.1):** encrypt a synthetic fixture with a password derived by a known rule, then assert the resolver tries **dictionary → rule → prompt** in order, caches the winner, and — critically — that **no password material appears in logs or exceptions** (log-capture assertion).

**Parser tests (C.2):** synthetic HDFC statement → assert normalized `transactions` (date, amount, direction, balance) match the generator's known ledger.

---

## 8. CI shape (GitHub Actions)

- **Default job** (`push` / `pr`): `setup-python@3.13` → install → `ruff check` → `pytest -m "not ocr and not llm and not local_statements"`. Offline, no secrets. Dependency cache on.
- **OCR job** (manual / scheduled): installs Tesseract, runs `pytest -m ocr`.
- **Guard job** (always): the security assertions in § 9.
- Coverage reported but thresholds start modest and ratchet up; we don't gate on a vanity number before the code exists.

---

## 9. Security assertions as tests (muneem-specific, must-pass)

These encode the DESIGN § 5 standing rules as failing-build checks:

- **No sensitive paths tracked.** A test runs `git ls-files` and fails if anything under `testdata/statements/`, `testdata/private/`, `*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, `token*`, `.env`, or `password_rules.*` is tracked.
- **Cloud-LLM category gate.** Calling the cloud-LLM client with a category in {bank, cc, broker, mf, insurance} raises/refuses; only {promo, …explicitly-approved} are allowed. A test asserts the refusal.
- **Log redaction.** Feed synthetic account numbers / balances / a known password through the logging path; assert they are masked in captured output.
- **Token storage.** Token persistence goes through the `keyring` abstraction (mocked in tests); a test asserts nothing is written to a plaintext file on disk.

---

## 10. Action items surfaced by this grounding

Small, real follow-ups discovered while building the answer key (tracked, not silently fixed):

1. **Establish the 6 unverified answer-key rows** (A.4) — OCR + manual confirmation.
2. **Fix the corpus README mislabel**: `airasia-1.pdf` is *Air India Express*, and the "no PII beyond recipient email" note understates that the recipient (`Ayush Raina`) is a third party present in message bodies.
3. **Ligature normalization** is a hard requirement, not a nicety — wire NFKC into the extractor before code matching.

---

## 11. Definition of done (testing) for Track A

`expected.yaml` committed with every verified row; **T1 recall + precision = 100%** in default CI; **T3 negatives extract nothing**; **T2 passes locally with OCR**; idempotency + the § 9 security guards green. That is the bar for calling the promo "forgotten deals" feature trustworthy.

### 62. assistant (2026-05-30T17:25:34.665Z)

"""Local paths and configuration.

muneem is local-first: config lives in the OS config dir, data (DB + staging)
in the OS data dir. Nothing here touches the repository or the network, and no
secrets are stored here — those go through :mod:`muneem.secrets` (the keychain).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from platformdirs import PlatformDirs

_dirs = PlatformDirs(appname="muneem", appauthor=False)

CONFIG_DIR = Path(_dirs.user_config_dir)
DATA_DIR = Path(_dirs.user_data_dir)
CONFIG_FILE = CONFIG_DIR / "config.toml"
DB_PATH = DATA_DIR / "muneem.db"
STAGING_DIR = DATA_DIR / "staging"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    """Resolved local paths plus any values from ``config.toml``."""

    config_dir: Path = CONFIG_DIR
    data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR
    config_file: Path = CONFIG_FILE
    db_path: Path = DB_PATH
    staging_dir: Path = STAGING_DIR
    values: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


def load_config() -> Config:
    """Load configuration, reading ``config.toml`` if it exists. Read-only."""
    values: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if CONFIG_FILE.is_file():
        with CONFIG_FILE.open("rb") as fh:
            values = tomllib.load(fh)
    return Config(values=values)


def ensure_dirs() -> None:
    """Create the local config/data/staging dirs if missing. Never touches the repo."""
    for directory in (CONFIG_DIR, DATA_DIR, STAGING_DIR):
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

### 64. assistant (2026-05-30T17:25:39.869Z)

"""Secret storage via the OS keychain.

OAuth tokens and cached statement passwords are stored here (Windows Credential
Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service), never in the repo, on disk in
plaintext, or in logs. See DESIGN.md section 5.

This is the thin foundation used later by ingestion (token) and unlocking
(per-sender cached password) — see docs/ROADMAP.md milestones B.1 and C.1.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import keyring
from keyring.errors import PasswordDeleteError

_SERVICE = "muneem"


def get_secret(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the stored secret, or None if absent."""
    return keyring.get_password(_SERVICE, name)


def set_secret(name: str, value: str) -> None:
    """Store (or replace) a secret in the OS keychain."""
    keyring.set_password(_SERVICE, name, value)


def delete_secret(name: str) -> None:
    """Delete a secret if present; a no-op if it is not."""
    try:
        keyring.delete_password(_SERVICE, name)
    except PasswordDeleteError:
        pass

"""The ``muneem`` command-line interface.

Milestone 0 ships ``--version`` and ``info``. Subcommands for the pipeline
(``fetch``, ``ingest``, ``offers``, ``txns``) land with their milestones.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import typer

from muneem import __version__
from muneem.config import load_config

app = typer.Typer(
    add_completion=False,
    help="muneem — a local-first personal-finance bookkeeper.",
    no_args_is_help=True,
)


def _version_callback(value: bool) -> None:
    if value:
        typer.echo(f"muneem {__version__}")
        raise typer.Exit()


@app.callback()
def main(
    version: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--version",
        callback=_version_callback,
        is_eager=True,
        help="Show the muneem version and exit.",
    ),
) -> None:
    """muneem command-line interface."""


@app.command()
def info() -> None:
    """Show resolved local paths (no secrets, no sensitive data)."""
    cfg = load_config()
    present = "present" if cfg.config_file.is_file() else "absent"
    typer.echo(f"muneem {__version__}")
    typer.echo(f"config dir : {cfg.config_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"data dir   : {cfg.data_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"db path    : {cfg.db_path}")
    typer.echo(f"staging    : {cfg.staging_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"config file: {cfg.config_file} ({present})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

### 72. assistant (2026-05-30T17:25:54.458Z)

"""Security guard: no sensitive paths may be tracked in git.

Encodes DESIGN.md section 5 ("Nothing sensitive ever in git") and docs/TESTING.md
section 9 as a failing-build assertion. If this test fails, something that must
stay local has been committed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES = ("testdata/statements/", "testdata/private/")
FORBIDDEN_SUFFIXES = (".db", ".sqlite", ".sqlite3", ".env", ".pem", ".key")
FORBIDDEN_NAMES = (
    "token.json",
    "token.pickle",
    "credentials.json",
    "password_rules.yaml",
    "password_rules.yml",
    "password_rules.json",
    "passwords.txt",
)


def _tracked_files() -> list[str]:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files"],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return [line.strip() for line in out.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]


def test_no_sensitive_paths_tracked():
    offenders = []
    for path in _tracked_files():
        low = path.lower()
        if (
            low.startswith(FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES)
            or low.endswith(FORBIDDEN_SUFFIXES)
            or Path(path).name.lower() in FORBIDDEN_NAMES
        ):
            offenders.append(path)

## The testing strategy, grounded in your actual corpus

Rather than hand-wave, I extracted the text layer from all 10 promo PDFs and rendered a sample. The corpus stratifies cleanly into the test tiers, and the real data exposed gotchas worth designing around:

| Tier | What it tests | Real fixtures |
|---|---|---|
| **T1** text-layer codes | deterministic, no OCR | `dataquest → JS231sz`, `makemytrip-2 → EARLYBIRDDEAL` |
| **T2** image-only codes | OCR required | `swiggy → CTSWIGGYUX` |
| **T3** no-code negatives | precision / no hallucination | `flipkart` |
| **T4** unverified | answer key TBD | the other 6 (don't invent codes) |

Gotchas now baked into the plan: **`ﬀ` ligatures** in the text layer ("Oﬀer" ≠ "Offer" → needs NFKC), **relative/countdown expiry** ("Ends Today", "Last few hours" → resolve against email date), and a **synthetic-fixture** path so the *sensitive* HDFC parser gets CI coverage without real statements.

Two **doc-vs-reality discrepancies** I found and logged (TESTING.md §10, not silently fixed): `airasia-1.pdf` is actually an **Air India Express** mailer (README mislabels it AirAsia), and the corpus recipient is **Ayush Raina** — a third party from the prototype, present in message bodies — not you. Both non-sensitive, but the corpus README overstates "no PII."

## Why I paused here

Milestone 0 sets the conventions everything else inherits (package layout, toolchain, CLI shape), so it's the natural point for a glance before I stack more on top. I went with **pip + setuptools** (not the roadmap's tentative `uv`, which isn't installed) — lowest lock-in, works with `uv pip` too; trivial to switch if you'd rather.

### 96. assistant (2026-05-30T17:58:08.376Z)

"""PDF text extraction (the deterministic, born-digital path).

Ports the Email-Mining insight — PyMuPDF (``fitz``) for the text layer — into a
proper module. NFKC normalization is applied because the real corpus returns
ligatures (e.g. U+FB00 'ﬀ') that would otherwise break naive matching.

Image extraction + dedup + OCR (for codes rasterized into banners, e.g. Swiggy's
``CTSWIGGYUX``) is the image tier and lands with the OCR work — see docs/TESTING.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import fitz


@dataclass
class Extracted:
    """The result of reading a PDF's text layer."""

    path: Path
    sha256: str
    page_count: int
    text: str


def _normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """NFKC-normalize so ligatures fold to ASCII (U+FB00 'ﬀ' -> 'ff')."""
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)


def file_sha256(path: Path | str) -> str:
    """Stream the file and return its hex SHA-256 (used for document dedup)."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def extract(pdf_path: Path | str) -> Extracted:
    """Extract and normalize the full text layer of a PDF."""
    path = Path(pdf_path)
    parts: list[str] = []
    with fitz.open(str(path)) as doc:
        page_count = doc.page_count
        for page in doc:
            parts.append(page.get_text("text"))
    return Extracted(
        path=path,
        sha256=file_sha256(path),
        page_count=page_count,
        text=_normalize("".join(parts)),
    )

### 98. assistant (2026-05-30T17:58:17.430Z)

"""Deterministic promo-offer extraction from normalized email text.

Precision-first: we anchor on an explicit "code" cue and validate the captured
token, so a promo email with *no* code (e.g. Flipkart's GOAT-sale banner)
correctly yields nothing rather than a hallucinated code. Codes rasterized into
images (e.g. Swiggy) are out of scope here — that's the OCR tier.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

_CODE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:coupon\s+code|promo\s*code|use\s+code|using\s+code|code)\b\s*[:\-]?\s*([A-Za-z0-9]{4,20})",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_EXPIRY_PATTERNS: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]] = [
    (re.compile(r"\bends today\b", re.I), "relative"),
    (re.compile(r"\blast few hours\b", re.I), "relative"),
    (re.compile(r"\bfinal day\b", re.I), "relative"),
    (re.compile(r"\bbefore\s+[A-Z][a-z]+\s+\d{1,2}\w*", re.I), "absolute"),
    (re.compile(r"\bvalid\s+(?:till|until|through)\b[^\n]{0,40}", re.I), "absolute"),
    (re.compile(r"\bexpir\w*\b[^\n]{0,40}", re.I), "absolute"),
]


def _looks_like_code(token: str) -> bool:
    """A code-like token has a digit, or is all-caps and reasonably long."""
    if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in token):
        return True
    return token.isupper() and len(token) >= 5


@dataclass
class OfferFields:
    codes: list[str]
    expiry_raw: str | None
    expiry_type: str | None


def extract_offer(text: str) -> OfferFields:
    """Pull promo code(s) and a best-effort expiry phrase from email text."""
    codes: list[str] = []
    for match in _CODE_RE.finditer(text):
        token = match.group(1)
        if _looks_like_code(token) and token not in codes:
            codes.append(token)

    expiry_raw: str | None = None
    expiry_type: str | None = None
    for pattern, etype in _EXPIRY_PATTERNS:
        found = pattern.search(text)
        if found:
            expiry_raw = found.group(0).strip()
            expiry_type = etype
            break

    return OfferFields(codes=codes, expiry_raw=expiry_raw, expiry_type=expiry_type)

### 100. assistant (2026-05-30T17:58:29.377Z)

"""Local SQLite store: the ``documents`` and ``offers`` slice of the schema.

This is the minimal slice the promo spine needs (ROADMAP A.2). The full schema
(accounts, transactions, holdings, merchants, items) grows with later milestones.
``documents.sha256`` is UNIQUE so re-ingesting the same file is a no-op.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

_SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    source        TEXT NOT NULL,
    external_id   TEXT,
    sender        TEXT,
    subject       TEXT,
    received_date TEXT,
    doc_type      TEXT,
    sha256        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    path          TEXT,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'parsed',
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS offers (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    merchant    TEXT,
    promo_code  TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    expiry_raw  TEXT,
    expiry_type TEXT,
    redeemed    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    source_text TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_offers_document ON offers(document_id);
"""


@contextmanager
def connect(db_path: Path | str) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """Open a connection (commit on success, always close). Parent dirs created."""
    path = str(db_path)
    if path != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


def init_db(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    """Create tables if absent and stamp the schema version."""
    conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
    conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {SCHEMA_VERSION}")


def get_document_by_sha(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sha256: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
    return conn.execute("SELECT * FROM documents WHERE sha256 = ?", (sha256,)).fetchone()


def insert_document(conn: sqlite3.Connection, **fields: object) -> int:
    cols = ", ".join(fields)
    placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in fields)
    cur = conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO documents ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})",
        tuple(fields.values()),
    )
    return int(cur.lastrowid)


def insert_offer(conn: sqlite3.Connection, **fields: object) -> int:
    cols = ", ".join(fields)
    placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in fields)
    cur = conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO offers ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})",
        tuple(fields.values()),
    )
    return int(cur.lastrowid)


def list_offers(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
    return conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT o.id, o.merchant, o.promo_code, o.expiry_raw, o.description,
               d.external_id, d.path
        FROM offers o
        JOIN documents d ON d.id = o.document_id
        ORDER BY o.id
        """
    ).fetchall()

### 102. assistant (2026-05-30T17:58:47.572Z)

"""The ``muneem`` command-line interface.

Track A ships the promo spine: ``ingest`` a PDF into the local store and
``offers list`` to read back what was found. Pipeline subcommands for ingestion
(``fetch``) and statements (``txns``) land with their milestones.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import typer

from muneem import __version__
from muneem.config import load_config

app = typer.Typer(
    add_completion=False,
    help="muneem — a local-first personal-finance bookkeeper.",
    no_args_is_help=True,
)
offers_app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help="Work with extracted offers.")
app.add_typer(offers_app, name="offers")


def _version_callback(value: bool) -> None:
    if value:
        typer.echo(f"muneem {__version__}")
        raise typer.Exit()


@app.callback()
def main(
    version: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--version",
        callback=_version_callback,
        is_eager=True,
        help="Show the muneem version and exit.",
    ),
) -> None:
    """muneem command-line interface."""


@app.command()
def info() -> None:
    """Show resolved local paths (no secrets, no sensitive data)."""
    cfg = load_config()
    present = "present" if cfg.config_file.is_file() else "absent"
    typer.echo(f"muneem {__version__}")
    typer.echo(f"config dir : {cfg.config_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"data dir   : {cfg.data_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"db path    : {cfg.db_path}")
    typer.echo(f"staging    : {cfg.staging_dir}")
    typer.echo(f"config file: {cfg.config_file} ({present})")


@app.command()
def ingest(
    pdf: Path = typer.Argument(
        ..., exists=True, dir_okay=False, readable=True, help="Path to a PDF to ingest."
    ),
    doc_type: str = typer.Option("promo", help="Document category."),
    db: Path | None = typer.Option(None, help="SQLite path (defaults to the local data dir)."),
) -> None:
    """Extract a PDF and store its document + any offers in the local DB."""
    from muneem import db as dbmod
    from muneem.extract import extract
    from muneem.offers import extract_offer

    db_path = db or load_config().db_path
    ex = extract(pdf)
    fields = extract_offer(ex.text)

    with dbmod.connect(db_path) as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
        existing = dbmod.get_document_by_sha(conn, ex.sha256)
        if existing is not None:
            typer.echo(f"already ingested (doc {existing['id']}): {pdf.name}")
            return
        doc_id = dbmod.insert_document(
            conn,
            source="file",
            external_id=pdf.name,
            doc_type=doc_type,
            sha256=ex.sha256,
            path=str(pdf.resolve()),
            status="parsed",
        )
        for code in fields.codes:
            dbmod.insert_offer(
                conn,
                document_id=doc_id,
                promo_code=code,
                expiry_raw=fields.expiry_raw,
                expiry_type=fields.expiry_type,
                source_text=ex.text[:2000],
            )

    summary = ", ".join(fields.codes) if fields.codes else "none"
    typer.echo(f"ingested {pdf.name} (doc {doc_id}); {len(fields.codes)} offer(s): {summary}")


@offers_app.command("list")
def offers_list(
    db: Path | None = typer.Option(None, help="SQLite path (defaults to the local data dir)."),
) -> None:
    """List extracted offers."""
    from muneem import db as dbmod

    db_path = db or load_config().db_path
    if not Path(db_path).exists():
        typer.echo("no offers yet (database not created).")
        return

    with dbmod.connect(db_path) as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
        rows = dbmod.list_offers(conn)

    if not rows:
        typer.echo("no offers found.")
        return
    for row in rows:
        who = row["merchant"] or row["external_id"] or "?"
        when = f" — expires {row['expiry_raw']}" if row["expiry_raw"] else ""
        typer.echo(f"[{row['id']}] {who}: {row['promo_code']}{when}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

"""Regression over the committed promo corpus, driven by expected.yaml.

Covers the deterministic tiers only: T1 (text-layer codes must be recovered) and
T3 (no-code emails must yield nothing). T2 (image-only, needs OCR) and T4
(unverified) are intentionally excluded here — see docs/TESTING.md sections 3-4.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

from muneem.extract import extract
from muneem.offers import extract_offer

CORPUS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "testdata" / "promo-emails"
ANSWERS = yaml.safe_load((CORPUS / "expected.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

DETERMINISTIC = sorted(
    name
    for name, spec in ANSWERS.items()
    if spec.get("verified") and spec.get("tier") in {"T1", "T3"}
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", DETERMINISTIC)
def test_promo_codes_match_answer_key(name):
    spec = ANSWERS[name]
    got = extract_offer(extract(CORPUS / name).text).codes
    if spec["code_location"] == "none":
        assert got == [], f"{name}: expected no codes, got {got}"
    else:
        for code in spec["codes"]:
            assert code in got, f"{name}: expected {code!r} in {got}"

On muneem, Avi wants implementation delivered as **one PR per roadmap work item**, and chose **"merge as I go"**: self-merge each PR to `main` once it is green (ruff + pytest pass, verified locally), then build the next item from `main`. Squash-merge, delete the branch. Planning/docs PRs are merged before code PRs begin.

**Why:** solo personal repo optimizing for velocity over pre-merge review; local verification + CI is the quality gate, and post-hoc review/revert is acceptable.

**How to apply:** after finishing a work item, verify locally (install, `ruff check`, `pytest`, exercise the real CLI), open a PR with a clear body, squash-merge it yourself, sync `main`, and continue — don't wait for manual review unless asked. The roadmap milestones in `docs/ROADMAP.md` are the work-item list.
