I got some detailed feedback on the code and overall design. i want to share the code and implementation level feedback for now. Since this is going to be a commercial grade personal tool, the bar for code quality is super high. So please seriously assess the entire feedback and push back where its not immediately necessary or unfit. Please make sure to start making changes on these and merge the PRs while ensuring the test coverage is >80% and CIs keep passing. Try to not make a gigantic PR but understandable if you need to. I will share the design feedback after you are done making the changes.

"
Code-Level / Implementation (reliability, correctness, maintainability, security hardening):
• Error handling & exception hygiene (critical). Replace broad except Exception as exc: raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to parse {pdf_path}: {exc}") (seen in axis/au/hdfc paths) with a small hierarchy (MuneemError, ParseError (with non-sensitive context only), UnlockError, EncryptedDatabaseError already good). Never put raw statement text, passwords, or full paths with PII into exception messages that might be logged. Add specific handling for pdfplumber/pypdf/pdfminer failures, corrupt PDFs, unexpected layouts. Every external call (pdf libs, keyring, yaml, sql) must be wrapped with attribution of what failed.
• Introduce a logging + redaction module now. Even before full structured logs, centralize all output that could contain sensitive data. Add provenance (which layer/mapping/profile produced a parse) to every row and document it.
• Type safety. Add mypy (or pyright) to dev deps + CI (strict). Many places use loose object, bare dict, sqlite3.Row without protocols. Cell = object, family build callables, etc. benefit from tighter contracts. Ruff is good but insufficient alone for commercial Python.
• Parser robustness & the known Axis gap. Invest in the clusterer (better line recovery, coverage for the May 2025 drop case, more synthetic matrices that reproduce real vintage drift). Make coordinate clustering and engine output carry richer diagnostics (without values) for eval. Add property-based tests (hypothesis) over synthetic matrices for the verifier/engine. Increase synthetic PDF coverage in synthpdf.py to hit more header variants, wrapped narrations, multi-account sections, SUMMARY drift.
• PDF library surface area. You have pdfminer.six (text), pypdf (decrypt), pdfplumber (tables+words), pypdfium2 (render). Audit overlap and pin exact versions. Ensure password is always passed through and never persisted. Consider whether a thinner extraction abstraction would reduce surface.
• Secrets / password / key handling hardening. password_rules.yaml loader has a deprecation path — good. Add validation (no empty passwords, quote-numeric reminder). Ensure _remember and keychain JSON lists are size-capped or aged. Add tests that assert no password material appears in any log, exception, or stdout even on failure paths (already partially done; make exhaustive). Test the full hybrid order + caching + --no-prompt + legacy CWD warning.
• DB / crypto invariants (already strong — make them stronger). The test_db_invariants.py + crypto tests + schema lock are excellent. Add: WAL checkpoint + backup API tests, rekey/rotation path tests (even if deferred), performance guard on large ledgers, explicit test that connect_encrypted on a plaintext file always raises the helpful message. Harden the encrypt_database temp-file cleanup and verification.
• CLI & UX for trust. txns list output is minimal/raw. Add columns for status/provenance, filters (date range, amount, account), and a "verify" subcommand that re-runs reconciliation on stored rows. ingest and eval must never echo statement content. Add machine-readable output (JSON) behind a flag.
• Testing gaps to close for commercial bar.
  • Full end-to-end with mocked providers (no real OAuth).
  • More negative/adversarial fixtures (bad dates, transposed digits, ligatures, zero-amount rows, multi-currency, footer/header pollution).
  • Snapshot/golden for unified extracted text per issuer vintage (non-sensitive synthetic only).
  • Fuzzing or mutation testing on the verifier (a single off-by-one in reconcile must be caught).
  • Explicit tests for every security assertion in TESTING.md §9 (some exist; make the log-redaction and cloud-LLM-category-gate assertions ironclad).
  • Headless Linux keyring fallback tests.
• Hygiene & process. Add mypy + (optional) bandit/safety to lint. Consider a small CONTRIBUTING or "how to add a bank" that points to onboarding-a-bank.md + eval. Pin the exact synthpdf layout expectations so clusterer changes are deliberate. Expand the pre-push gate to include the license and hygiene tests explicitly if not already covered by pytest.
• Smaller code smells. Remove dead back-compat aliases where possible (or clearly mark). Centralize date/money regexes more. Make safe_amount vs parse_amount distinction (0.00 handling) documented in one place. Add __version__ from git or build metadata instead of hardcoded 0.0.1. Consistent use of pathlib vs str. Consider a small models or domain layer if per-bank tables grow.
• Performance / scale (personal but real statements can be 30-100 pages). Profile large PDFs. Image dedup (MD5 + SSIM heritage) should be wired for statement chrome once L3 or heavy OCR lands. Memory-map or streaming where pdfplumber holds everything.
• Docs & attribution. Produce the promised docs/parser-notes-hdfc.md (and per-issuer) as part of D.3. Keep "memory" references (hdfc-parser-tech-decision etc.) either in-repo or removed. Maintain the decision log in ROADMAP §1.

Overall assessment: The foundation (security invariants, reconciliation-as-oracle philosophy, profiles-as-data, hygiene automation, non-sensitive regression corpus with ground truth) is already at or above commercial bar for a personal tool. The parser architecture is thoughtful and the right shape for the "formats change yearly" reality of Indian banks. The main risks to commercial viability are (1) silent or brittle parsing on real drift (mitigated by oracle but needs the regression CI and clustering recovery), (2) absence of operational visibility (logging, backup, health), and (3) incomplete vertical slice (fetch + unified schema + 100% real-data precision on the first banks).
"

6	``AUBANK_PROFILE`` — this parser is mostly the DB wiring. No statement content is logged here.

13

17	from .base import StatementParser

19	from .savings import SavingsParse, parse_savings
20	from .validation import Confidence
21	
22	
23	def parse_au_savings(pdf_path: Path, password: str | None = None) -> SavingsParse:
24	    """Parse an AU Bank savings statement via the shared engine-driven path."""
25	    return parse_savings(pdf_path, AUBANK_PROFILE, password)
26	
27	
28	@register_parser
29	class AUParser(StatementParser):
30	    def can_handle(self, text: str, sender: str | None = None, subject: str | None = None) -> bool:
31	        if sender and "aubank" in sender.lower():
32	            return True
33	        low = (text or "").lower()
34	        return "au small finance bank" in low or "aubank" in low
35	
36	    def parse_and_insert(
37	        self, pdf_path: Path, conn: sqlite3.Connection, doc_id: int, password: str | None = None
38	    ) -> int:
39	        """Persist a savings parse **only if it reconciles**; otherwise store nothing."""

41	            parsed = parse_au_savings(pdf_path, password)

43	            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to parse AU statement {pdf_path}: {exc}") from exc
44	
45	        if not parsed.verified:

47	                "UPDATE documents SET status = ? WHERE id = ?",
48	                (Confidence.UNRECONCILED.value, doc_id),
49	            )
50	            return 0

59	                particulars=r.narration,

61	                credit=r.credit,
62	                balance=r.balance,
63	            )

1	"""Password rule loader for statement decryption (hybrid strategy support).
2	
3	Prefers the user config dir (via platformdirs, e.g. ~/.config/muneem/password_rules.yaml
4	on Linux) for real rules. Falls back to legacy CWD "password_rules.yaml" (common during
5	dev) with a DeprecationWarning. **Never commit real rules or the file itself** — `.gitignore`
6	blocks `password_rules.*`.
7	
8	See DESIGN.md §8.2, CLAUDE.md security rules, and docs/ingesting-statements.md for the file
9	format. Entries are either ``<bank>: <password>`` or a top-level ``candidates: [..]`` list.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import warnings
15	from pathlib import Path
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	import yaml
19	
20	from muneem.config import CONFIG_DIR
21	
22	
23	def _load_rules() -> dict[str, Any]:
24	    """Load the rules dict from the config dir (preferred) or legacy CWD file; ``{}`` if absent.
25	
26	    Resolution order:
27	    1. ``<config_dir>/password_rules.yaml``  (recommended location)
28	    2. ``./password_rules.yaml``  (legacy, emits DeprecationWarning)
29	    """
30	    for path, is_legacy in (
31	        (CONFIG_DIR / "password_rules.yaml", False),
32	        (Path("password_rules.yaml"), True),
33	    ):
34	        if path.exists():
35	            if is_legacy:
36	                warnings.warn(
37	                    "Loading password_rules from CWD (./password_rules.yaml) is deprecated. "
38	                    f"Move it to {CONFIG_DIR / 'password_rules.yaml'} for future-proofing. "
39	                    "See docs and CLAUDE.md (never commit real password material).",
40	                    DeprecationWarning,
41	                    stacklevel=3,
42	                )
43	            with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
44	                return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
45	    return {}
46	
47	
48	def get_password_for_bank(bank_name: str) -> str | None:
49	    """Return the password (or derived rule string) for a bank, or ``None``."""
50	    val = _load_rules().get(bank_name)
51	    return str(val) if val else None
52	
53	
54	def candidate_passwords() -> list[str]:
55	    """Every configured password to try as an unlock candidate, **bank-agnostic**.
56	
57	    The ingest path resolves the password *before* it knows the issuer (it needs the decrypted
58	    text to pick a parser), so it tries all configured passwords. Collects each per-bank value
59	    plus any entries under a top-level ``candidates:`` list; order preserved, de-duplicated.
60	    Quote numeric passwords in the YAML so leading zeros survive.
61	    """
62	    rules = _load_rules()
63	    collected: list[str] = []
64	    for key, val in rules.items():
65	        if key == "candidates" and isinstance(val, list):
66	            collected.extend(str(v) for v in val if v not in (None, ""))
67	        elif isinstance(val, str | int | float):
68	            collected.append(str(val))

### 1129. assistant (2026-06-02T17:20:47.348Z)

"""muneem's exception hierarchy.

Every error muneem raises derives from :class:`MuneemError`, so callers can catch the whole family
with one `except`. Two rules for messages on these exceptions, because they may end up in logs:

1. **Only non-sensitive context.** A file *name* is acceptable (it's the user's own machine), but
   never raw statement text, passwords, balances, or account numbers. Use
   :mod:`muneem.redaction` helpers to sanitise anything derived from a document.
2. **Chain the cause.** Raise with ``raise ParseError(...) from exc`` so the original traceback is
   available for local debugging while the muneem-level message stays clean.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class MuneemError(Exception):
    """Base class for all errors raised by muneem."""


class ParseError(MuneemError):
    """A document could not be parsed (corrupt PDF, unexpected layout, extraction failure).

    Carries only non-sensitive context (e.g. the file name and the failing stage) — never the
    statement contents or the underlying library's message verbatim.
    """


class UnlockError(MuneemError):
    """A password-protected document could not be unlocked (no working password, bad input)."""


class EncryptedDatabaseError(MuneemError):
    """The encrypted ledger could not be opened — wrong key, missing SQLCipher binding, or a
    plaintext file where an encrypted one was expected."""

### 1131. assistant (2026-06-02T17:21:03.118Z)

"""Redaction helpers — keep sensitive data out of logs, exceptions, and stdout.

muneem aggregates the user's whole financial life, so a balance, account number, or password that
slips into a log line or an exception message is a real incident. These helpers produce *safe*
representations for diagnostics. They are deliberately conservative: it is better to over-mask a
diagnostic string than to leak one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

# Long digit runs look like account / card / customer numbers.
_ACCOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"\d{9,}")
# Money-like: Indian or Western grouping with a decimal, or a plain N.NN amount.
_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"\d{1,3}(?:,\d{2,3})+(?:\.\d{1,2})?|\d+\.\d{2}")
# Digit runs in a filename that may be PII (DOB, account suffix, customer id).
_FILENAME_DIGITS_RE = re.compile(r"\d{4,}")


def redact_filename(path: str | Path) -> str:
    """Return a file's *name only* (never the full path), with long digit runs masked.

    The full path can expose the user's home/account layout, and a bare basename can still carry PII
    (Indian statement names are often ``Name_DDMMYYYY.pdf``), so digit runs of 4+ are masked. Keeps
    enough of the name to be useful in a diagnostic.
    """
    name = Path(str(path)).name
    return _FILENAME_DIGITS_RE.sub(lambda m: "#" * len(m.group()), name)


def redact_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Mask account-number-like and money-like substrings in free text (e.g. before logging).

    A backstop for accidental leaks — code should already pass sanitised context; this catches what
    slips through. Returns the input unchanged if there is nothing to mask.
    """
    if not text:
        return text
    masked = _AMOUNT_RE.sub("‹amt›", text)
    masked = _ACCOUNT_RE.sub("‹acct›", masked)
    return masked


def mask_secret(secret: str | None) -> str:
    """A non-reversible placeholder for a password/key — its length only, never the value."""
    if not secret:
        return "‹none›"
    return f"‹secret:{len(secret)} chars›"

### 1133. assistant (2026-06-02T17:21:35.469Z)

"""Central, redaction-aware logging.

Use ``get_logger(__name__)`` instead of the stdlib ``logging.getLogger`` so every muneem logger
carries a :class:`RedactingFilter`. The filter scrubs money-/account-like substrings from each
record as a backstop — code should still pass already-sanitised context (see
:mod:`muneem.redaction`); this is defense-in-depth so an accidental sensitive f-string cannot leak.

muneem stays library-style: we attach the filter but do **not** configure handlers or levels (the
application / CLI owns that), so importing muneem never hijacks the root logger.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

from muneem.redaction import redact_text


class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
    """A logging filter that masks sensitive substrings in the formatted message."""

    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        try:
            message = record.getMessage()
        except Exception:  # never drop a record just because formatting failed
            return True
        redacted = redact_text(message)
        if redacted != message:
            record.msg = redacted
            record.args = ()
        return True


_filtered: set[str] = set()


def get_logger(name: str) -> logging.Logger:
    """Return a logger that redacts sensitive substrings from its records (idempotent)."""
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
    if name not in _filtered:
        logger.addFilter(RedactingFilter())
        _filtered.add(name)
    return logger

"""Every parser wraps an unexpected failure in a clean, non-leaking ``ParseError``.

A PDF library can raise with statement text in its message; the muneem-level error must expose only
a redacted filename (no full path, no statement contents, no PII digits), while preserving the

import pytest

from muneem import db as dbmod
from muneem.errors import ParseError
from muneem.parsers import au, axis, hdfc

# Looks like statement text a pdf lib might surface in an exception message.
_SECRET = "ACCT 998877665544 balance 1,23,456.78"


def _raiser(*_a, **_k):
    raise ValueError(_SECRET)


CASES = [
    ("muneem.parsers.axis.parse_axis_savings", axis.AxisParser),
    ("muneem.parsers.axis.parse_axis_cc", axis.AxisCreditCardParser),
    ("muneem.parsers.au.parse_au_savings", au.AUParser),
    ("muneem.parsers.hdfc.parse_statement", hdfc.HDFCParser),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("patch_target, parser_cls", CASES)
def test_parse_failures_become_clean_parseerror(monkeypatch, patch_target, parser_cls):
    monkeypatch.setattr(patch_target, _raiser)
    parser = parser_cls()
    pdf = Path("/home/avi/statements/Avi_Dullu_28022026.pdf")
    with dbmod.connect(":memory:") as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
        with pytest.raises(ParseError) as ei:
            parser.parse_and_insert(pdf, conn, 1, password="pw")
    msg = str(ei.value)
    assert _SECRET not in msg and "998877665544" not in msg  # no statement text
    assert "/home/avi" not in msg and "statements" not in msg  # no full path
    assert "28022026" not in msg  # PII digits masked
    assert isinstance(ei.value.__cause__, ValueError)  # original cause preserved

1	"""Decrypt password-protected statement PDFs (Stage 2).
2	
3	Uses pypdf (BSD-3-Clause) — permissive, pure-Python. Implements the hybrid
4	password strategy from DESIGN.md § 8.2: try a candidate dictionary first, then
5	fall back to an interactive prompt. The working password is returned so the
6	caller can cache it in the OS keychain (muneem.secrets); **it is never logged**.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import shutil
12	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
13	from dataclasses import dataclass
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	import pypdf
17	
18	
19	@dataclass
20	class UnlockResult:
21	    ok: bool
22	    method: str | None  # "plaintext" | "candidate" | "prompt"
23	    password: str | None  # working password — do NOT log; None if plaintext/failed
24	    output_path: Path | None  # decrypted copy, if a destination was given
25	
26	
27	def is_encrypted(path: Path | str) -> bool:
28	    return pypdf.PdfReader(str(path)).is_encrypted
29	
30	
31	def password_works(path: Path | str, password: str) -> bool:
32	    reader = pypdf.PdfReader(str(path))
33	    if not reader.is_encrypted:
34	        return True
35	    try:
36	        return reader.decrypt(password) != pypdf.PasswordType.NOT_DECRYPTED
37	    except Exception:
38	        return False
39	
40	
41	def write_decrypted(path: Path | str, password: str | None, dest: Path | str) -> Path:
42	    """Write a decrypted copy of the PDF to dest (password may be '' for plaintext)."""
43	    src = Path(path)
44	    dest = Path(dest)
45	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
46	    reader = pypdf.PdfReader(str(src))
47	    if reader.is_encrypted:
48	        reader.decrypt(password or "")
49	    writer = pypdf.PdfWriter()
50	    writer.append(reader)
51	    with open(dest, "wb") as fh:
52	        writer.write(fh)
53	    return dest
54	
55	
56	def unlock(
57	    path: Path | str,
58	    candidates: Iterable[str] = (),
59	    prompt_fn: Callable[[], str | None] | None = None,
60	    max_prompts: int = 3,
61	    dest: Path | str | None = None,
62	) -> UnlockResult:
63	    """Hybrid unlock: plaintext? -> candidate dictionary -> interactive prompt.
64	
65	    If dest is given and unlock succeeds, a decrypted copy is written there. The
66	    working password is returned in the result but must never be logged.
67	    """
68	    src = Path(path)
69	    if not is_encrypted(src):
70	        out = Path(shutil.copyfile(src, dest)) if dest else None
71	        return UnlockResult(True, "plaintext", None, out)
72	
73	    tried: set[str] = set()
74	    for pw in candidates:
75	        if pw in tried:
76	            continue
77	        tried.add(pw)
78	        if password_works(src, pw):
79	            out = write_decrypted(src, pw, dest) if dest else None
80	            return UnlockResult(True, "candidate", pw, out)
81	
82	    if prompt_fn is not None:
83	        for _ in range(max_prompts):
84	            pw = prompt_fn()
85	            if not pw:
86	                break
87	            if password_works(src, pw):
88	                out = write_decrypted(src, pw, dest) if dest else None
89	                return UnlockResult(True, "prompt", pw, out)
90	
91	    return UnlockResult(False, None, None, None)

1	"""muneem's exception hierarchy.
2	
3	Every error muneem raises derives from :class:`MuneemError`, so callers can catch the whole family
4	with one `except`. Two rules for messages on these exceptions, because they may end up in logs:
5	
6	1. **Only non-sensitive context.** A file *name* is acceptable (it's the user's own machine), but
7	   never raw statement text, passwords, balances, or account numbers. Use
8	   :mod:`muneem.redaction` helpers to sanitise anything derived from a document.
9	2. **Chain the cause.** Raise with ``raise ParseError(...) from exc`` so the original traceback is
10	   available for local debugging while the muneem-level message stays clean.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	
16	class MuneemError(Exception):
17	    """Base class for all errors raised by muneem."""
18	
19	
20	class ParseError(MuneemError):
21	    """A document could not be parsed (corrupt PDF, unexpected layout, extraction failure).
22	
23	    Carries only non-sensitive context (e.g. the file name and the failing stage) — never the
24	    statement contents or the underlying library's message verbatim.
25	    """
26	
27	
28	class UnlockError(MuneemError):
29	    """A password-protected document could not be unlocked (no working password, bad input)."""
30	
31	
32	class EncryptedDatabaseError(MuneemError):
33	    """The encrypted ledger could not be opened — wrong key, missing SQLCipher binding, or a
34	    plaintext file where an encrypted one was expected."""

### 1208. assistant (2026-06-02T17:31:10.404Z)

"""Secret storage via the OS keychain.

OAuth tokens, cached statement passwords, and the DB encryption key are stored here (Windows
Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service), never in the repo, on disk in plaintext, or
in logs. See DESIGN.md section 5.

External-call discipline (every keyring call is wrapped with attribution):
- **read** (:func:`get_secret`) is *graceful* — a missing or unavailable backend returns ``None``
  (absence is a valid state; this also keeps headless CI happy).
- **write** (:func:`set_secret`) is *loud* — a failure raises :class:`~muneem.errors.KeychainError`,
  because silently losing a write (e.g. the DB key) would be dangerous. The secret *name* is
  included for diagnosis; the value never is.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import keyring
from keyring.errors import KeyringError, PasswordDeleteError

from muneem.errors import KeychainError

_SERVICE = "muneem"


def get_secret(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the stored secret, or ``None`` if absent or the keychain is unavailable."""
    try:
        return keyring.get_password(_SERVICE, name)
    except KeyringError:
        return None


def set_secret(name: str, value: str) -> None:
    """Store (or replace) a secret in the OS keychain. Raises KeychainError on failure."""
    try:
        keyring.set_password(_SERVICE, name, value)
    except KeyringError as exc:
        # Name only — never the value — in the message (it may be a password or the DB key).
        raise KeychainError(f"could not store secret {name!r} in the OS keychain") from exc


def delete_secret(name: str) -> None:
    """Delete a secret if present; a no-op if it is not (or the keychain is unavailable)."""
    try:
        keyring.delete_password(_SERVICE, name)
    except (PasswordDeleteError, KeyringError):
        pass

"""The OS-keychain wrappers: graceful read, attributed (value-free) write, swallowed delete.

The autouse conftest fixture swaps ``muneem.secrets`` for an in-memory store, so we capture the
*real* wrapper functions at import time and drive them by patching the underlying ``keyring`` lib.
"""

import keyring
import pytest
from keyring.errors import KeyringError

import muneem.secrets as secretsmod
from muneem.errors import KeychainError

# Captured before the autouse keychain fixture rebinds the module attributes per-test.
_real_get = secretsmod.get_secret
_real_set = secretsmod.set_secret
_real_delete = secretsmod.delete_secret


def test_get_secret_returns_none_when_keyring_unavailable(monkeypatch):
    def boom(service, name):
        raise KeyringError("no backend")

    monkeypatch.setattr(keyring, "get_password", boom)
    assert _real_get("anything") is None  # graceful: absence, not a crash


def test_get_secret_returns_the_value(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(keyring, "get_password", lambda s, n: "v" if n == "k" else None)
    assert _real_get("k") == "v"
    assert _real_get("missing") is None


def test_set_secret_raises_keychain_error_with_name_but_not_value(monkeypatch):
    def boom(service, name, value):
        raise KeyringError("locked")

    monkeypatch.setattr(keyring, "set_password", boom)
    with pytest.raises(KeychainError) as ei:
        _real_set("db-key", "super-secret-value")
    msg = str(ei.value)
    assert "db-key" in msg  # the name is safe to surface
    assert "super-secret-value" not in msg  # the value must NEVER appear


def test_delete_secret_swallows_keyring_errors(monkeypatch):
    def boom(service, name):
        raise KeyringError("nope")

    monkeypatch.setattr(keyring, "delete_password", boom)
    _real_delete("k")  # must not raise

import warnings

import pytest

from muneem import password_rules as pr
from muneem.errors import ConfigError


@pytest.fixture
def dirs(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Distinct config dir and working dir so we can exercise the legacy-CWD fallback."""
    cfg = tmp_path / "config"
    cfg.mkdir()
    work = tmp_path / "work"
    work.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setattr(pr, "CONFIG_DIR", cfg)
    monkeypatch.chdir(work)
    return cfg, work


def test_candidate_passwords_dedup_and_preserve_quoted_numeric(dirs):
    cfg, _ = dirs
    (cfg / "password_rules.yaml").write_text(
        "hdfc: '0012'\naxis: SUNE\ndupe: SUNE\ncandidates:\n  - '0012'\n  - EXTRA\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    cands = pr.candidate_passwords()
    assert "0012" in cands  # leading zero survives because it was quoted
    assert cands.count("SUNE") == 1 and cands.count("0012") == 1  # de-duplicated
    assert "EXTRA" in cands  # top-level candidates: list collected too


def test_get_password_for_bank(dirs):
    cfg, _ = dirs
    (cfg / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("hdfc: SECRET1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert pr.get_password_for_bank("hdfc") == "SECRET1"
    assert pr.get_password_for_bank("nope") is None


def test_missing_file_yields_empty(dirs):
    assert pr.candidate_passwords() == []
    assert pr.get_password_for_bank("x") is None


def test_legacy_cwd_file_emits_deprecation_warning(dirs):
    _, work = dirs
    (work / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("hdfc: X\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning):
        assert pr.get_password_for_bank("hdfc") == "X"


def test_config_dir_takes_precedence_over_cwd(dirs):
    cfg, work = dirs
    (cfg / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("hdfc: FROMCONFIG\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (work / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("hdfc: FROMCWD\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error")  # config-dir hit must NOT warn
        assert pr.get_password_for_bank("hdfc") == "FROMCONFIG"


def test_malformed_yaml_raises_configerror_without_leaking_contents(dirs):
    cfg, _ = dirs
    (cfg / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("hdfc: 'SUPERSECRETPW\n", encoding="utf-8")  # unterminated
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError) as ei:
        pr.candidate_passwords()
    assert "SUPERSECRETPW" not in str(ei.value)  # contents never surface
    assert "password_rules.yaml" in str(ei.value)


def test_non_mapping_yaml_raises_configerror(dirs):
    cfg, _ = dirs
    (cfg / "password_rules.yaml").write_text("- just\n- a\n- list\n", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError):
        pr.candidate_passwords()

211	def encrypt_database(db_path: Path | str, key: str) -> int:
212	    """Migrate a plaintext SQLite ledger to an encrypted one in place, via ``sqlcipher_export``.
213	
214	    The original is preserved as ``<name>.plaintext.bak`` for the caller to verify and then
215	    securely delete (it still holds the cleartext data). Returns the number of user tables
216	    copied. Raises :class:`EncryptedDatabaseError` if ``db_path`` is not a plaintext SQLite file.
217	    """
218	    import sqlcipher3
219	
220	    path = Path(db_path)
221	    if not is_plaintext_sqlite(path):
222	        raise EncryptedDatabaseError(
223	            f"{path.name} is not a plaintext SQLite database (already encrypted or missing)"
224	        )
225	
226	    enc_tmp = path.with_name(path.name + ".enc.tmp")
227	    enc_tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
228	    src = sqlcipher3.connect(str(path))  # open the plaintext source (no key)
229	    try:
230	        src_tables = src.execute(
231	            "SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'"
232	        ).fetchone()[0]
233	        target = str(enc_tmp).replace("\\", "/")  # SQL string literal: forward slashes
234	        src.execute(f"ATTACH DATABASE '{target}' AS encrypted KEY \"x'{key}'\"")
235	        src.execute("SELECT sqlcipher_export('encrypted')")
236	        src.execute("DETACH DATABASE encrypted")
237	    finally:
238	        src.close()
239	
240	    # Verify the encrypted copy BEFORE the destructive swap: it must open with the key, pass an
241	    # integrity check, and carry every table across. (The plaintext .bak is kept regardless, so a
242	    # failed check is recoverable — but we refuse to swap in a bad file.)
243	    with connect(str(enc_tmp), key=key) as check:
244	        integrity = check.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0]
245	        ntables = check.execute(
246	            "SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'"
247	        ).fetchone()[0]
248	    if integrity != "ok" or ntables != src_tables:
249	        enc_tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
250	        raise EncryptedDatabaseError(
251	            f"encryption migration verification failed for {path.name} "
252	            f"(integrity={integrity!r}, tables {ntables}/{src_tables}); original left untouched"
253	        )
254	
255	    backup = path.with_name(path.name + ".plaintext.bak")
256	    backup.unlink(missing_ok=True)
257	    path.rename(backup)
258	    enc_tmp.rename(path)
259	    _harden_permissions(str(path))

### 1310. assistant (2026-06-02T17:48:03.433Z)

"""Crypto operations on the encrypted ledger: key rotation, encrypted backup, migration temp
cleanup, correctness at size, and the plaintext-refusal guidance — plus their CLI commands.

Offline, fabricated data only; the autouse conftest fixture keeps the real keychain untouched.
"""

import sqlite3

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("sqlcipher3")

from typer.testing import CliRunner  # noqa: E402

from muneem import db as dbmod  # noqa: E402
from muneem import db_key  # noqa: E402
from muneem.cli import app  # noqa: E402

runner = CliRunner()

KEY_A = "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
KEY_B = "ffeeddccbbaa99887766554433221100ffeeddccbbaa99887766554433221100"


def _seed_encrypted(path, key, n=3):
    with dbmod.connect(path, key=key) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, amount REAL)")
        conn.executemany("INSERT INTO t (amount) VALUES (?)", [(float(i),) for i in range(n)])


# --- rekey / rotation -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_rekey_changes_the_key_and_keeps_data(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    _seed_encrypted(p, KEY_A, n=5)
    dbmod.rekey_database(p, KEY_A, KEY_B)
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError):  # old key no longer opens it
        with dbmod.connect(p, key=KEY_A):
            pass
    with dbmod.connect(p, key=KEY_B) as conn:  # new key works, data intact
        assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM t").fetchone()[0] == 5


def test_rekey_with_wrong_current_key_raises(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    _seed_encrypted(p, KEY_A)
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError):
        dbmod.rekey_database(p, KEY_B, KEY_A)


# --- encrypted backup -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_backup_is_encrypted_and_intact(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    _seed_encrypted(p, KEY_A, n=4)
    dest = tmp_path / "backup" / "led.bak.db"
    dbmod.backup_database(p, dest, KEY_A)
    assert dest.exists() and not dbmod.is_plaintext_sqlite(dest)  # backup stays encrypted
    with dbmod.connect(dest, key=KEY_A) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM t").fetchone()[0] == 4
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError):  # wrong key can't read the backup
        with dbmod.connect(dest, key=KEY_B):
            pass


def test_backup_with_wrong_key_raises(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    _seed_encrypted(p, KEY_A)
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError):
        dbmod.backup_database(p, tmp_path / "b.db", KEY_B)


# --- migration cleanup + correctness at size + plaintext refusal ------------------------------


def test_encrypt_database_cleans_temp_on_failure(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    con = sqlite3.connect(p)
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)")
    con.commit()
    con.close()

    def boom(*_a, **_k):  # fail the post-export verification open
        raise RuntimeError("boom during verify")

    monkeypatch.setattr(dbmod, "_open_encrypted", boom)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        dbmod.encrypt_database(p, KEY_A)
    assert not (tmp_path / "led.db.enc.tmp").exists()  # partial temp removed
    assert dbmod.is_plaintext_sqlite(p)  # original left untouched


def test_encrypted_ledger_handles_a_larger_table(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    with dbmod.connect(p, key=KEY_A) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, amount REAL)")
        conn.executemany("INSERT INTO t (amount) VALUES (?)", [(float(i),) for i in range(2000)])
    with dbmod.connect(p, key=KEY_A) as conn:
        total = conn.execute("SELECT SUM(amount) FROM t").fetchone()[0]
        cnt = conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE amount >= 1000").fetchone()[0]
    assert cnt == 1000 and total == float(sum(range(2000)))


def test_connect_encrypted_plaintext_message_points_to_db_encrypt(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "led.db"
    con = sqlite3.connect(p)
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER)")
    con.commit()
    con.close()
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError) as ei:
        with dbmod.connect_encrypted(p):
            pass
    assert "muneem db encrypt" in str(ei.value)  # actionable guidance, not a cryptic error


# --- CLI: db rotate-key / db backup -----------------------------------------------------------


def _new_encrypted_ledger(path):
    with dbmod.connect_encrypted(path) as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
        dbmod.insert_document(conn, source="file", sha256="s", status="parsed")


def test_db_rotate_key_cli(tmp_path):
    led = tmp_path / "ledger.db"
    _new_encrypted_ledger(led)
    old = db_key.peek_key()
    res = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "rotate-key", "--db", str(led)])
    assert res.exit_code == 0, res.output
    new = db_key.peek_key()
    assert new and new != old
    with dbmod.connect(led, key=new) as conn:  # opens under the new key
        assert dbmod.get_document_by_sha(conn, "s") is not None
    with pytest.raises(dbmod.EncryptedDatabaseError):  # old key no longer works
        with dbmod.connect(led, key=old):
            pass


def test_db_backup_cli(tmp_path):
    led = tmp_path / "ledger.db"
    _new_encrypted_ledger(led)
    dest = tmp_path / "led.backup.db"
    res = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "backup", str(dest), "--db", str(led)])
    assert res.exit_code == 0, res.output
    assert dest.exists() and not dbmod.is_plaintext_sqlite(dest)
    with dbmod.connect(dest, key=db_key.peek_key()) as conn:
        assert dbmod.get_document_by_sha(conn, "s") is not None


def test_db_rotate_key_refuses_when_no_encrypted_ledger(tmp_path):
    res = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "rotate-key", "--db", str(tmp_path / "nope.db")])
    assert res.exit_code == 1 and "db encrypt" in res.output

74	    ``entries`` is an ordered list of ``(debit, credit, balance)``; ``debit`` and

### 1341. assistant (2026-06-02T17:53:58.674Z)

"""Property-style fuzzing of the reconciliation verifier — deterministic (seeded), no new dep.

The verifier is muneem's truth oracle: an off-by-one in the balance walk or the total identity would
silently let mislabeled rows through. These tests generate many random *consistent* ledgers and
assert the oracles accept them, then perturb a single value past the tolerance and assert the oracles
catch it. A one-line slip in the reconcile arithmetic fails here.
"""

import random

import pytest

from muneem.parsers.concepts import ConceptRow
from muneem.parsers.validation import reconcile_running_balance, reconcile_total


def _consistent_ledger(rng: random.Random, n: int, opening: float):
    """Build a random clean ledger of ``n`` rows; return (rows, closing_balance)."""
    rows: list[ConceptRow] = []
    bal = opening
    for _ in range(n):
        amt = round(rng.uniform(0.01, 5000.0), 2)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            bal = round(bal - amt, 2)
            rows.append(ConceptRow(txn_date="01/01/2026", narration="x", debit=amt, balance=bal))
        else:
            bal = round(bal + amt, 2)
            rows.append(ConceptRow(txn_date="01/01/2026", narration="x", credit=amt, balance=bal))
    return rows, bal


def _entries(rows):
    return [(r.debit, r.credit, r.balance) for r in rows]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(60))
def test_consistent_ledger_always_reconciles(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    opening = round(rng.uniform(0, 100_000), 2)
    rows, closing = _consistent_ledger(rng, rng.randint(2, 40), opening)
    assert reconcile_running_balance(_entries(rows)).ok
    assert reconcile_total(rows, opening=opening, closing=closing)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(60))
def test_single_balance_perturbation_is_caught_by_the_walk(seed):
    rng = random.Random(10_000 + seed)
    opening = round(rng.uniform(0, 100_000), 2)
    rows, closing = _consistent_ledger(rng, rng.randint(2, 40), opening)
    i = rng.randrange(len(rows))
    r = rows[i]
    rows[i] = ConceptRow(  # corrupt one balance by more than the tolerance
        txn_date=r.txn_date, narration=r.narration, debit=r.debit, credit=r.credit,
        balance=round((r.balance or 0.0) + 1.0, 2),
    )
    assert not reconcile_running_balance(_entries(rows)).ok


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(60))
def test_total_oracle_catches_a_wrong_closing_bookend(seed):
    rng = random.Random(20_000 + seed)
    opening = round(rng.uniform(0, 100_000), 2)
    rows, closing = _consistent_ledger(rng, rng.randint(2, 40), opening)
    assert reconcile_total(rows, opening=opening, closing=closing)
    assert not reconcile_total(rows, opening=opening, closing=round(closing + 1.0, 2))

### 1363. assistant (2026-06-02T18:01:56.259Z)

# feedbackJune2026 — Architectural Review: Response & Incorporation Plan

> **Status: DRAFT for iteration.** This is my analysis of the June-2026 architectural review — what
> to accept, what to push back on (with reasons), and *the right way* to incorporate the rest.
> Nothing here is implemented yet; we iterate → finalize → then implement. Open decisions are
> flagged **🔓 DECISION** and must be resolved with Avi before code locks them in.
>
> Author's note (attribution): claims about current code are grounded in the repo as of `main`
> after PRs #34–#40. Where I infer or recommend, I say so.

---

## 0. Framing — what "commercial-grade" means *here*

muneem is **paid, but single-user, local-first, and lifelong**: one person's entire financial life,
on their own machine, for years. So the bar is **correctness · zero-leak · auditability ·
recoverability · maintainability-by-one**. It is **not** multi-tenant SaaS. That distinction drives
several push-backs below: the right move is to be *bulletproof at single-user scale*, not to import
enterprise machinery (heavy ORMs, distributed anything, a web tier) that adds surface without
serving the actual risk. "High bar" = fewer moving parts, each provably correct and recoverable.

Two non-negotiables carry over from CLAUDE.md and stay load-bearing in everything below:
1. **No sensitive data leaves the machine** without explicit per-category, per-session approval.
2. **No open architectural decision gets silently locked** by code. This doc proposes; Avi disposes.

---

## 1. Corrections — three premises in the review are already stale

The review is strong, but three items were **done in the recent code-quality pass** and should be
re-scoped from "needed" to "extend / verify":

| Review claim | Reality (as of `main`) | What actually remains |
|---|---|---|
| "currently zero logging in src/" | **False now.** `muneem/log.py` (`get_logger` + `RedactingFilter`) + `muneem/redaction.py` landed in **#36**, wired into `cli`, with masking tests (`test_redaction`, `test_log`). | Structured (JSON/logfmt) output + **broad adoption** across modules + per-stage leak tests. The *foundation* exists. |
| "muneem db backup (proper Online Backup API, not naive cp)" | **Done in #39.** `backup_database()` uses the SQLite Online Backup API (WAL-safe), destination keyed → encrypted backup. | A documented restore runbook; optional *recovery-key* backups (see §2). |
| "key rotation scaffolding (the deferred passphrase path)" | **Rotation done in #39.** `rekey_database()` + `muneem db rotate-key` (keychain-first with rollback). | The **passphrase path** specifically — but reframed as **recovery**, not just "stronger" (see §2). |

Also already in place (so the review's "table-stakes" list is largely satisfied): SQLCipher
encryption-at-rest (#34), schema-lock + DB-invariant tripwires (#34), pre-commit secret guard,
license allowlist, **mypy** + **ruff** + **80% coverage gate** in CI and the pre-push hook (#38/#40),
verifier property-fuzz (#40). The engineering-hygiene floor is commercial-grade *today*.

---

## 2. 🔥 The biggest risk the review *under-weights*: key-loss / disaster recovery (P0)

Encrypting the ledger at rest (correctly!) created a **catastrophic single point of failure** that
none of the ten bullets names directly:

> The 256-bit DB key lives only in the OS keychain. **`muneem db backup` encrypts the backup with the
> same key.** So if the keychain is lost — OS reinstall, profile/Credential-Manager corruption, dead
> machine, new laptop — the ledger **and every backup** are *permanently unrecoverable*.

For a tool whose entire pitch is "hold my whole financial life for years," this outranks most of the
listed features. It must be solved **before** we accumulate real, irreplaceable history.

**The right way (reframe the deferred "passphrase mode" from security → recovery):**
- Keep the random DB key (fast, full-entropy) as the working key.
- Add a **recovery wrapper**: encrypt the DB key under a user passphrase (Argon2id, OWASP params)
  and store that wrapped blob in a `recovery.json` the user backs up **off-machine** (password
  manager / printed). Losing the keychain → restore the key from passphrase + recovery file.
- And/or `muneem db export-key` — prints the raw key **once**, with loud warnings, for the user's
  password manager. Simpler; less safe-by-default.
- Optionally let `db backup --recovery-key` write a backup under the passphrase-derived key, so a
  backup is restorable even with the keychain gone.
- Ship a **`docs/recovery.md` runbook**: "keychain lost," "move to a new machine," "verify a backup."

**🔓 DECISION:** which recovery model — (a) passphrase-wrapped recovery file *(recommended)*, (b)
one-time key export, (c) both. Pick before storing real numbers long-term.

---

## 3. Point-by-point: verdict · the right way · dependencies

Verdicts: **✅ Accept** · **🟡 Accept-with-changes** · **⛔ Push back** · **✔️ Largely done**.

### P1 — Structured, redacted logging (D.1) · 🟡 Accept-with-changes
Premise stale (see §1). **Right way:** build on `log.py`/`redaction.py`; add a structured formatter
(logfmt or JSON — 🔓 minor decision), adopt `get_logger(__name__)` across `parsers/`, `db`, `unlock`,
`ingestion` at sensible levels; keep `RedactingFilter` as the *backstop*, not the primary control
(code passes already-redacted context). **Tests:** feed synthetic sensitive values through *each
stage* and assert masking (extend the #36 tests). The other half of D.1 — *idempotent, resumable
re-runs* — is a **pipeline** concern (staging dir + `documents.status`), partly separable; don't
conflate. **Priority: high, low-risk — Phase A.**

### P2 — Two-layer regression CI · ✅ Accept (already the plan)
Layer 1 (synthetic full-pipeline via `synthpdf.py`) exists (`test_regression_synth.py`); expand it
for more HDFC/Axis/AU header variants + bookend drift (this also absorbs the deferred "adversarial
synthpdf fixtures" follow-up from the code pass). Layer 2 (self-hosted runner over real, gitignored
statements; passwords from `password_rules.yaml`, **never** GitHub secrets) is decided/deferred.
**Caveat to record:** a self-hosted runner executes CI on Avi's personal machine — fine for a
no-external-contributor repo, but note it runs only when the machine is on, and never enable it for
forked PRs. **🔓 DECISION:** confirm self-hosted-runner acceptance. **Phase D.**

### P3 — Unified storage + provenance/confidence · ✅ Accept — but **design before code** 🔓
This is *the* central architectural decision; the per-bank tables are an explicit fidelity crutch.
**Right way:** canonical `accounts` / `transactions` / `holdings` (+ later `merchants`/`items`), where
**every `transactions` row carries provenance**: `source_document_id`, `parser`, `parser_version`,
`mapping_layer` (L0/profile/L2/L3), `confidence`, `reconciled`. That provenance *is* the auditability
a paid ledger needs. **Migration, not rip-out:** parsers dual-write (per-bank table *and* canonical)
or a backfill migration converts them; keep per-bank as **views** for debugging/fidelity. The
schema-lock test makes this safe to evolve. **🔓 DECISION:** the shape — (a) one wide `transactions`
table with nullable family-specific columns, (b) core table + per-family side tables, (c) core +
JSON `extra`. I lean **(b)** (clean, queryable, no JSON-in-SQL foot-guns). **Phase B — gates P7/P8.**

### P4 — L3 vision fallback + golden evals · 🟡 Accept-with-changes (sequence!)
Decision stands (DeepSeek-OCR-3B, MIT, 4-bit+SDPA on the 2070S, reconcile-gated, self-consistency
resampling). **Push-back on ordering:** L3 should come **after D.3** — the eval writeup that
*characterizes where the deterministic ladder actually breaks*. Building a fallback before we know
its target failure modes is guessing. So: **D.3 eval first → then L3.** Golden sets (local +
synthetic now; cloud eval-only, approval-gated) extend `muneem eval`. **Phase E (after D.3).**

### P5 — Resolve/time-box parked decisions (§8.3 LLM locality, §8.5 merchant canon) · ✅ Accept
These stay parked until a milestone *forces* them, and surface to Avi with the hardware/latency
constraints first. **Hard rule restated:** no cloud path for bank/CC/broker data, even
experimentally, without per-session approval + redaction + a test gate. Merchant canon (§8.5) is
downstream of P3+P8. **Governance item — not a build; revisit at the phase boundary.**

### P6 — Versioned, tested schema migrations + `docs/schema.md` · 🟡 Accept — but ⛔ **not Alembic**
Accept the need; **reject Alembic** (it drags SQLAlchemy — heavy, ORM-shaped — against muneem's
deliberate raw-`sqlite3`, stdlib-light design). **Right way:** a tiny hand-rolled runner — numbered
`migrations/NNN_*.py|sql` applied in order inside the keyed connection, recorded in a
`schema_migrations` table, each with an **idempotency/up-checksum**, gated by the `user_version`
pragma. Pair with the existing schema-**lock** test (drift tripwire) → versioned + tested + enforced.
Add a living `docs/schema.md`. Note: migrations run *inside* the encrypted connection — fine, but the
runbook must cover "migrate then re-verify reconciliation." **Phase A (precedes P3's migrations).**

### P7 — Ingestion completeness + `muneem fetch` · 🟡 Accept — but ⛔ re-sequence
**Push-back on "before heavy parser work":** the parser core is already *proven* (HDFC 6/6, AU 4/4,
Axis 6/7) and the user supplies statements manually today. `fetch` is **automation/convenience, not
correctness** — it doesn't unblock parser accuracy or the whole-finance vision; **storage
unification (P3) does.** So: **P3 before P7.** What *is* cheap and should happen immediately:
explicitly mark Outlook/IMAP attachment paths **experimental/deferred** in code + docs (the mypy
override already treats them as such) so no one mistakes scaffolding for support. Then build `fetch`
(incremental `historyId`/`deltaLink`, sender allowlist + "financial document" heuristics, staging →
`documents` rows as `locked`/`unparsed`, robust dedup) as **Phase F**. The fast bit (mark
experimental) is **Phase A**.

### P8 — Tier-2 transaction semantics + merchant canonicalization · ✅ Accept (downstream)
Strictly **after P3** (needs the canonical schema) and needs **real receipt data** to expose the mess
(don't design merchant canon in the abstract). Counterparty/merchant extraction + fuzzy match +
a user-editable **override table**; itemized receipts (Swiggy/Amazon) likewise. **Phase G.**

### P9 — Observability / ops surface · 🟡 Accept (partly done; pull recovery forward)
Done: `db backup` (Online Backup API), `db rotate-key`, `db status` (#39). **Right way for the rest:**
`muneem verify` (re-run reconciliation over *stored* rows — a cheap, high-value integrity audit that
also exercises provenance), `export` (CSV/JSON for the user's own analysis — explicitly **redaction-
exempt** since it's the user's own data to their own disk, but never to stdout/logs), `txns` filters
(date/amount/account/status), light analytics. **Crucially, the recovery model (§2) belongs here but
is P0 — pull it into Phase A, not "later."** Document backup/restore + "keychain lost." **Phase A
(recovery) + Phase H (the rest).**

### P10 — Packaging / distribution / reproducibility · 🟡 Accept-with-changes
- **Lockfile** (uv.lock or pip-tools `requirements*.txt`): ✅ yes — reproducibility is real for a tool
  with a compiled dep (sqlcipher3). **Phase A.**
- **Cross-platform CI matrix** (Windows + macOS, not just ubuntu): ✅ **high value, under-rated** —
  the dev box is Windows, and the secret backends genuinely differ (DPAPI vs Secret Service vs
  Keychain) and sqlcipher3 wheels are per-OS. This directly de-risks "works on my machine" for the
  one machine that matters. **Phase A.**
- **SBOM in CI** (CycloneDX): 🟡 reasonable for paid software but **time-box / low-urgency** — it
  serves a distribution/audit story we don't have yet. Do it near first external distribution, not
  now. **Phase H+.**
- **Local web UI:** ⛔ defer — CLI stays authoritative; a web tier is new attack surface + scope for
  no current need. Revisit only if a real UX gap appears.

---

## 4. Proposed sequencing (dependency-ordered)

> Rule of thumb: **recoverability + foundation first; then the one big schema decision; then
> everything that depends on it.** Each phase is shippable and individually PR-able.

- **Phase A — Foundation & recovery (low-risk, high-leverage):** §2 **recovery model (P0)** ·
  finish structured-logging adoption (P1) · hand-rolled migration runner + `docs/schema.md` (P6) ·
  lockfile + cross-platform CI matrix (P10) · mark Outlook/IMAP experimental (P7-fast).
- **Phase B — 🔓 Unified schema decision + migration (P3).** The gating design workshop. Nothing
  whole-finance proceeds cleanly until this lands.
- **Phase C — Instrument family** (equity/MF/ETF/bond events) on the unified schema + new
  `FamilySpec`/oracle (P3 cont.).
- **Phase D — Regression CI Layer 2 (self-hosted) + the D.3 eval writeup** (P2) — also tells us where
  L3 is actually needed.
- **Phase E — L3 vision fallback + golden evals (P4),** informed by D.3.
- **Phase F — `muneem fetch` + ingestion completeness (P7).**
- **Phase G — Tier-2 semantics + merchant canonicalization (P8),** on real receipt data.
- **Phase H — Remaining ops surface (verify/export/filters/analytics) (P9) + SBOM (P10).**
- **Parked/governance throughout:** §8.3, §8.5 (P5) — surface at their forcing milestones.

---

## 5. 🔓 Open decisions to settle before coding (so nothing gets silently locked)

1. **Recovery / key-loss model** (§2) — passphrase-wrapped recovery file *(rec.)* vs key-export vs both.
2. **Unified schema shape** (P3) — wide table vs **core + per-family** *(rec.)* vs core + JSON extra;
   exact provenance/confidence columns.
3. **Migration mechanism** (P6) — hand-rolled runner *(rec.)* vs Alembic *(not rec.)*.
4. **Structured log format** (P1) — logfmt vs JSON.
5. **Self-hosted runner** (P2) — accept the run-CI-on-my-machine trade-off?
6. **Cross-platform support scope** (P10) — Windows+Linux first-class; macOS best-effort?
7. **Parked:** §8.3 sensitive-doc LLM locality, §8.5 merchant canonicalization — confirm still parked.

---

## 6. Push-back summary (explicit, with reasons)

- **Alembic → hand-rolled migrations.** Dep-minimization + raw-`sqlite3` design + the schema-lock
  already exists; Alembic's ORM weight buys nothing here.
- **"Ingestion before heavy parser work" → storage unification (P3) first.** Parser core is proven;
  `fetch` is convenience, not correctness. (But mark Outlook/IMAP experimental *now* — cheap.)
- **L3 before D.3 → reversed.** Characterize the deterministic ladder's failure modes *first*; don't
  build a fallback blind.
- **SBOM / web UI → time-box / defer.** Low urgency vs correctness + recoverability; web UI is
  unjustified surface for a single-user CLI tool.
- **Don't over-engineer for scale muneem doesn't have.** Single-user, local-first. Bulletproof beats
  big.
- **And the addition the review missed: key-loss recovery is P0** — above most of the feature list.

---

*Next step: Avi reviews → we settle §5's open decisions → I revise this doc to "FINAL" → implement
phase-by-phase, one PR per item, CI green and ≥80% coverage throughout.*

Drafted to **`docs/feedbackJune2026.md`** (uncommitted — it's a draft for us to iterate before it goes in). Here's the substance so you can react without opening it.

## How I read the review
It's strong and mostly right. I structured my response around: **correct what's stale → elevate the risk it missed → push back where warranted → sequence by dependency → flag what we must decide before coding.**

## Three premises are already stale (done in the recent pass)
- **"zero logging in src/"** — false now; the redaction-aware logger (`log.py` + `redaction.py`) landed in #36 with masking tests. What's left is *structured output + broad adoption*, not greenfield.
- **"need `db backup` (Online Backup API)"** and **"key rotation scaffolding"** — both **implemented in #39**. So those drop from "needed" to "done."

So the hygiene floor (encryption, schema-lock, mypy, ruff, 80% coverage gate, secret guards) is already commercial-grade.

## The big thing the review under-weights — I made it P0
**Key-loss = total, permanent data loss.** The DB key lives only in the keychain, and `db backup` encrypts backups with that *same* key — so a lost keychain (OS reinstall, dead machine, new laptop) destroys the ledger **and every backup**. For a "hold my finances for years" tool that outranks most of the feature list. I propose reframing the deferred "passphrase mode" from *stronger security* → *disaster recovery*: a passphrase-wrapped recovery file the user backs up off-machine, plus a `docs/recovery.md` runbook. **This needs to be solved before we accumulate real history.**

## Where I push back (with reasons)
- **Alembic → hand-rolled migrations.** Alembic drags in SQLAlchemy; muneem is deliberately raw-`sqlite3`/stdlib-light, and the schema-lock test already exists. A tiny numbered-migration runner fits.
- **"Ingestion before heavy parser work" → storage unification first.** The parser core is *proven*; `fetch` is convenience, not correctness. (But mark Outlook/IMAP experimental *now* — that's cheap.)
- **L3 vision before the D.3 eval → reversed.** Characterize where the deterministic ladder actually breaks *first*; don't build a fallback blind.
- **SBOM / local web UI → time-box / defer.** Low urgency vs correctness+recovery; a web tier is unjustified attack surface for a single-user CLI.
- **Don't over-engineer for scale muneem doesn't have** — single-user, local-first; bulletproof beats big.

## Where I fully agree (the right way, sequenced)
**Unified schema with per-row provenance + confidence (P3) is the central decision** and everything whole-finance depends on it — done as *migration with per-bank views*, not a rip-out. Then instrument family → regression-CI Layer 2 + D.3 → L3 → fetch → merchant canon. Cross-platform CI matrix (Win/macOS) I actually rate *higher* than the review did — the secret backends and sqlcipher3 wheels genuinely differ per-OS.

## Open decisions I need you on (so nothing locks silently)
1. **Recovery model** (passphrase-wrapped file ⭐ / key-export / both)
2. **Unified schema shape** (wide table / **core + per-family** ⭐ / core + JSON)

4. Structured log format (logfmt / JSON) · 5. Self-hosted runner OK? · 6. macOS first-class or best-effort? · 7. Confirm §8.3 / §8.5 still parked

### 1378. assistant (2026-06-03T17:10:08.758Z)

# muneem — Database schema (living document)

> **Schema version: 4** (stamped via `PRAGMA user_version`). The canonical DDL is
> `src/muneem/db.py:_SCHEMA`; this document mirrors it for humans. The shape is pinned by the
> **schema-lock test** (`tests/test_db_invariants.py`) — an accidental drift fails CI, and any
> deliberate change must update the lock (and, going forward, ship a migration) in the same PR.
>
> The database is **encrypted at rest** (SQLCipher; see [`encryption-at-rest.md`](./encryption-at-rest.md)).
> All tables below live inside the keyed connection; `:memory:` and tests use plaintext stdlib sqlite3.

## Current state & direction

Today muneem uses **per-issuer transaction tables** (`axis_transactions`, `axis_cc_transactions`,
`au_transactions`, `hdfc_transactions`) to preserve each statement's raw fidelity while parsers
mature. This is a deliberate, temporary crutch. The planned move (feedbackJune2026 **P3**, ROADMAP
step 5) is a **canonical `transactions` + `holdings` + `accounts`** model with per-row **provenance +
confidence**, with the per-bank tables retained as views/migration artifacts. That change is gated on
an open design decision (🔓 schema shape) and a hand-rolled migration runner (P6) — not yet done.

## Conventions
- Money columns are `REAL`. Dates are stored as `TEXT` (issuer-formatted strings, not normalised yet).
- Every per-bank txn table references `documents(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting a source
  document removes its rows. Foreign keys are enforced (`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` in `connect()`).
- `documents.sha256` is `UNIQUE` → re-ingesting the same file is a no-op (dedup).

## Tables

### `documents` — every ingested file
| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | PK |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL (e.g. `file`, `gmail`) |
| external_id | TEXT | provider id / filename |
| sender | TEXT | |
| subject | TEXT | |
| received_date | TEXT | |
| doc_type | TEXT | `promo`, `bank_statement`, … |
| sha256 | TEXT | NOT NULL, **UNIQUE** (dedup key) |
| path | TEXT | resolved local path |
| status | TEXT | NOT NULL default `parsed`; parsers set `reconciled` / `unreconciled` |
| created_at | TEXT | NOT NULL default `datetime('now')` |

### `offers` — promo codes (Track A)
| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | PK |
| document_id | INTEGER | NOT NULL → `documents(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| merchant, promo_code, description, expiry_raw, expiry_type | TEXT | |
| source | TEXT | NOT NULL default `text` (`text` = exact layer, `ocr` = approximate) |
| redeemed | INTEGER | NOT NULL default 0 |
| source_text | TEXT | provenance snippet |

Index: `idx_offers_document` on `offers(document_id)`.

### Per-bank transaction tables

**`axis_transactions`, `au_transactions`** (savings; identical shape):
`id` PK · `document_id` NOT NULL → documents (cascade) · `account_number` · `txn_date` · `value_date`
· `particulars` · `debit` REAL · `credit` REAL · `balance` REAL.

**`hdfc_transactions`** (savings):
`id` PK · `document_id` NOT NULL → documents (cascade) · `account_number` · `txn_date` · `value_date`
· `particulars` · `ref` · `withdrawal` REAL · `deposit` REAL · `closing_balance` REAL.

**`axis_cc_transactions`** (credit card — no running balance):
`id` PK · `document_id` NOT NULL → documents (cascade) · `account_number` · `txn_date` ·
`particulars` · `merchant_category` · `amount` REAL · `type` TEXT (`Cr`/`Dr`).

## Migrations

Current mechanism: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + the `user_version` pragma (`init_db`). Adequate for
the early additive phase. The commercial-bar plan (feedbackJune2026 **P6**) is a small **hand-rolled
migration runner** (numbered, ordered, checksummed migrations recorded in a `schema_migrations`
table; run inside the keyed connection) — **not Alembic** (keeps the raw-`sqlite3`, stdlib-light
design). Until then, schema changes are additive and gated by the schema-lock test. Keep this
document updated in lockstep with `_SCHEMA` whenever the lock changes.

### 1400. assistant (2026-06-03T17:21:47.468Z)

Strong agree on both — and they're the right *first* two because neither is blocked by the still-open schema-shape decision (#2), and the recovery model retires the **P0 key-loss risk** I flagged. Here's how I'd build each.

## Recovery model (passphrase-wrapped file)
Two commands, no secret ever stored in cleartext:
- **`muneem db setup-recovery`** — prompts for a passphrase (twice, no echo) → derives a wrapping key via a memory-hard KDF + random salt → wraps the keychain DB key with authenticated encryption → writes `muneem-recovery.json` (`{version, kdf:{salt,params}, nonce, ciphertext}` — no key, no passphrase). Warns: store it **off-machine**, use a strong passphrase, and that passphrase **+** file are both required.
- **`muneem db recover`** — prompts passphrase → derives the same key → decrypts the DB key → restores it to the keychain (so the ledger *and* any same-key backups open again). Wrong passphrase → AEAD auth fails → clean "wrong passphrase or corrupt file" (no leak).
- Defense-in-depth: the pre-commit guard will also block `*recovery*.json` from ever being committed.

This closes the gap where a lost keychain = permanent loss of the ledger and every backup.

## Migration runner (hand-rolled)
A tiny `muneem/migrations.py`: numbered, ordered migrations recorded in a `schema_migrations` table (version, name, applied_at, **checksum**); `init_db` delegates to it; the current v4 schema becomes the **baseline** migration; existing v4 DBs are detected and back-filled (no-op forward). It's deliberately **decoupled from the schema-*shape* decision** — it's the *mechanism*, so the first real data migration lands later with #2. Adding `schema_migrations` will trip the schema-lock — which is the point: that PR updates the lock as the explicit "allow."

## One fork I need you on
The recovery wrap needs an authenticated-encryption primitive, and Python's stdlib has no symmetric cipher — so it's either a small, standard dependency or a zero-dep reuse of our SQLCipher stack. This is genuinely your call given how dep-/license-conscious muneem is:

### 1407. assistant (2026-06-03T17:24:31.651Z)

"""Disaster recovery for the encrypted ledger — a passphrase-wrapped recovery file.

The DB key lives in the OS keychain (fast, full-entropy). If that keychain is ever lost — OS
reinstall, new machine, profile/Credential-Manager corruption — the ledger **and every same-key
backup** become permanently unrecoverable. This module lets the user wrap that key under a passphrase
they choose, into a recovery file they back up **off-machine**; with the file *and* the passphrase
they can restore the key into a fresh keychain.

Crypto: **Argon2id** (memory-hard KDF) derives a 256-bit wrapping key from the passphrase + a random
salt; **AES-256-GCM** (authenticated) wraps the DB key. The recovery file holds only
``{version, kdf params, salt, nonce, ciphertext}`` — never the key, never the passphrase. A wrong
passphrase fails the GCM authentication tag → a clean error, with no decryption oracle.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.argon2 import Argon2id

from muneem.errors import MuneemError

RECOVERY_VERSION = 1
_AAD = b"muneem-recovery-v1"  # binds the ciphertext to this format/version

# Argon2id parameters (memory in KiB). Conservative-but-real; the file stores them so they can be
# raised over time without breaking older recovery files.
_TIME_COST = 3
_MEMORY_KIB = 64 * 1024  # 64 MiB
_LANES = 4
_SALT_BYTES = 16
_NONCE_BYTES = 12
_KEY_BYTES = 32
_MIN_PASSPHRASE = 8


class RecoveryError(MuneemError):
    """A recovery file could not be created, or could not be opened (wrong passphrase / corrupt)."""


def _derive(passphrase: str, salt: bytes, *, time_cost: int, memory_kib: int, lanes: int) -> bytes:
    kdf = Argon2id(
        salt=salt,
        length=_KEY_BYTES,
        iterations=time_cost,
        lanes=lanes,
        memory_cost=memory_kib,
    )
    return kdf.derive(passphrase.encode("utf-8"))


def wrap_key(db_key: str, passphrase: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a JSON-serialisable recovery payload wrapping ``db_key`` under ``passphrase``."""
    if not passphrase or len(passphrase) < _MIN_PASSPHRASE:
        raise RecoveryError(f"recovery passphrase must be at least {_MIN_PASSPHRASE} characters")
    salt = os.urandom(_SALT_BYTES)
    nonce = os.urandom(_NONCE_BYTES)
    key = _derive(passphrase, salt, time_cost=_TIME_COST, memory_kib=_MEMORY_KIB, lanes=_LANES)
    ciphertext = AESGCM(key).encrypt(nonce, db_key.encode("utf-8"), _AAD)
    return {
        "version": RECOVERY_VERSION,
        "kdf": {
            "algo": "argon2id",
            "time_cost": _TIME_COST,
            "memory_kib": _MEMORY_KIB,
            "lanes": _LANES,
        },
        "salt": base64.b64encode(salt).decode(),
        "nonce": base64.b64encode(nonce).decode(),
        "ciphertext": base64.b64encode(ciphertext).decode(),
    }


def unwrap_key(payload: dict[str, Any], passphrase: str) -> str:
    """Recover the DB key from a recovery ``payload`` + ``passphrase``. Raises RecoveryError."""
    try:
        salt = base64.b64decode(payload["salt"])
        nonce = base64.b64decode(payload["nonce"])
        ciphertext = base64.b64decode(payload["ciphertext"])
        kdf = payload.get("kdf", {})
    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery file is malformed") from exc
    key = _derive(
        passphrase,
        salt,
        time_cost=int(kdf.get("time_cost", _TIME_COST)),
        memory_kib=int(kdf.get("memory_kib", _MEMORY_KIB)),
        lanes=int(kdf.get("lanes", _LANES)),
    )
    try:
        plain = AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, _AAD)
    except InvalidTag as exc:
        raise RecoveryError("wrong passphrase or corrupt recovery file") from exc
    return plain.decode("utf-8")


def write_recovery_file(path: Path | str, db_key: str, passphrase: str) -> Path:
    """Wrap ``db_key`` under ``passphrase`` and write the recovery file (owner-only perms)."""
    payload = wrap_key(db_key, passphrase)
    out = Path(path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        os.chmod(out, 0o600)
    except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - best-effort on platforms without POSIX perms
        pass
    return out


def read_recovery_file(path: Path | str, passphrase: str) -> str:
    """Read a recovery file and return the unwrapped DB key. Raises RecoveryError on any failure."""
    p = Path(path)
    try:
        payload = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise RecoveryError(f"could not read recovery file {p.name}") from exc
    return unwrap_key(payload, passphrase)

"""The passphrase-wrapped recovery file — round-trip, wrong-passphrase / corruption rejection,
no-secret-leak, and the CLI setup-recovery → (lost keychain) → recover flow. Fabricated keys only.
"""

import pytest
from typer.testing import CliRunner

from muneem import recovery
from muneem.recovery import RecoveryError

runner = CliRunner()

_DBKEY = "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff"
_PASS = "correct horse battery staple"


def test_wrap_unwrap_roundtrip():
    payload = recovery.wrap_key(_DBKEY, _PASS)
    assert recovery.unwrap_key(payload, _PASS) == _DBKEY


def test_wrong_passphrase_is_rejected():
    payload = recovery.wrap_key(_DBKEY, _PASS)
    with pytest.raises(RecoveryError):
        recovery.unwrap_key(payload, "a different passphrase")


def test_tampered_ciphertext_is_rejected():
    payload = recovery.wrap_key(_DBKEY, _PASS)
    payload["ciphertext"] = payload["ciphertext"][:-4] + "AAAA"  # flip the tail
    with pytest.raises(RecoveryError):
        recovery.unwrap_key(payload, _PASS)


def test_short_passphrase_refused():
    with pytest.raises(RecoveryError):
        recovery.wrap_key(_DBKEY, "short")


def test_recovery_file_leaks_neither_key_nor_passphrase(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "muneem-recovery.json"
    recovery.write_recovery_file(p, _DBKEY, _PASS)
    blob = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert _DBKEY not in blob and _PASS not in blob  # only the *wrapped* key is on disk
    assert recovery.read_recovery_file(p, _PASS) == _DBKEY  # but it round-trips


def test_read_missing_or_garbage_file_raises(tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(RecoveryError):
        recovery.read_recovery_file(tmp_path / "nope.json", _PASS)
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.json"
    bad.write_text("not json", encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(RecoveryError):
        recovery.read_recovery_file(bad, _PASS)


# --- CLI: setup-recovery -> lose keychain -> recover ------------------------------------------


def test_cli_setup_recovery_then_recover(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _isolate_keychain):
    pytest.importorskip("sqlcipher3")
    from muneem import db as dbmod
    from muneem import db_key
    from muneem.cli import app

    led = tmp_path / "ledger.db"
    with dbmod.connect_encrypted(led) as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
        dbmod.insert_document(conn, source="file", sha256="s", status="parsed")
    original = db_key.peek_key()
    assert original

    rec = tmp_path / "muneem-recovery.json"
    monkeypatch.setattr("getpass.getpass", lambda prompt="": _PASS)
    r1 = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "setup-recovery", "--out", str(rec)])
    assert r1.exit_code == 0, r1.output
    assert rec.exists()

    _isolate_keychain.clear()  # simulate a lost keychain
    assert db_key.peek_key() is None

    r2 = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "recover", str(rec), "--db", str(led)])
    assert r2.exit_code == 0, r2.output
    assert db_key.peek_key() == original  # key restored to the keychain
    with dbmod.connect(led, key=db_key.peek_key()) as conn:
        assert dbmod.get_document_by_sha(conn, "s") is not None


def test_cli_setup_recovery_passphrase_mismatch(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _isolate_keychain):
    from muneem import db as dbmod
    from muneem.cli import app

    with dbmod.connect_encrypted(tmp_path / "ledger.db") as conn:
        dbmod.init_db(conn)
    answers = iter(["passphrase-one", "passphrase-two"])
    monkeypatch.setattr("getpass.getpass", lambda prompt="": next(answers))
    r = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "setup-recovery", "--out", str(tmp_path / "r.json")])
    assert r.exit_code == 1 and "did not match" in r.output


def test_cli_recover_wrong_passphrase(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _isolate_keychain):
    from muneem.cli import app

    rec = tmp_path / "r.json"
    recovery.write_recovery_file(rec, _DBKEY, _PASS)
    monkeypatch.setattr("getpass.getpass", lambda prompt="": "the wrong passphrase entirely")
    r = runner.invoke(app, ["db", "recover", str(rec), "--db", str(tmp_path / "absent.db")])
    assert r.exit_code == 1 and ("wrong passphrase" in r.output or "corrupt" in r.output)

### 1455. assistant (2026-06-03T17:34:23.288Z)

"""Hand-rolled, versioned, checksummed schema migrations (feedbackJune2026 P6).

Deliberately **not Alembic** — muneem stays raw-`sqlite3` / stdlib-light. Migrations are an ordered
list; each is applied exactly once, *inside* the (possibly encrypted) connection, and recorded in a
``schema_migrations`` table with a checksum. The schema-lock test (`tests/test_db_invariants.py`)
pins the resulting shape, so accidental drift and deliberate changes both surface in review.

Model:
- **Baseline.** The current schema (`db._SCHEMA`, version `db.SCHEMA_VERSION`) is the *frozen*
  baseline — never edit it for new changes; add a migration instead. A fresh DB gets the baseline
  applied; a legacy DB created before this framework (tables present, no `schema_migrations`) is
  detected and its baseline row back-filled (no DDL re-run).
- **Forward migrations.** Entries in `MIGRATIONS` with ``version > baseline`` run in order. (None
  yet — the first lands with the unified-schema work, feedbackJune2026 P3.)

Known limitation (single-user, reviewed migrations): a crash *between* applying a migration's DDL and
recording it could require manual cleanup; per-migration transactions can be added when the first
non-trivial migration lands.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from muneem.errors import MigrationError

_SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (
    version    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    checksum   TEXT NOT NULL,
    applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Migration:
    """One forward migration: a version, a name, and the DDL to apply (run via executescript)."""

    version: int
    name: str
    sql: str

    @property
    def checksum(self) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(self.sql.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


# Forward migrations (version > baseline), applied in ascending order. Empty for now.
MIGRATIONS: list[Migration] = []


def _checksum(sql: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(sql.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _user_tables(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[str]:
    return [
        r[0]
        for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' "
            "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name != 'schema_migrations'"
        )
    ]


def _record(conn: sqlite3.Connection, version: int, name: str, checksum: str) -> None:
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, name, checksum) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
        (version, name, checksum),
    )


def run_migrations(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    *,
    baseline_sql: str,
    baseline_version: int,
    migrations: list[Migration] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Bring ``conn``'s schema up to date. Returns the resulting ``user_version``.

    Idempotent: re-running applies nothing already recorded. Raises :class:`MigrationError` if the
    frozen baseline's checksum no longer matches what was recorded (i.e. someone edited the baseline
    instead of adding a migration).
    """
    migrations = MIGRATIONS if migrations is None else migrations
    conn.executescript(_SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS)  # bookkeeping table first (idempotent)
    applied = {r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations")}
    current = conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
    baseline_checksum = _checksum(baseline_sql)

    if baseline_version in applied:
        recorded = conn.execute(
            "SELECT checksum FROM schema_migrations WHERE version = ?", (baseline_version,)
        ).fetchone()
        if recorded and recorded[0] != baseline_checksum:
            raise MigrationError(
                "baseline schema changed without a migration — add a migration instead of editing "
                "the frozen baseline (feedbackJune2026 P6)"
            )
    else:
        # Fresh DB → create the baseline; legacy DB (tables already present) → just record it.
        if not _user_tables(conn):
            conn.executescript(baseline_sql)
        _record(conn, baseline_version, "baseline", baseline_checksum)
        if current < baseline_version:
            conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {baseline_version}")
            current = baseline_version

    for migration in sorted(migrations, key=lambda m: m.version):
        if migration.version <= baseline_version or migration.version in applied:
            continue
        conn.executescript(migration.sql)
        _record(conn, migration.version, migration.name, migration.checksum)
        conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {migration.version}")
        current = migration.version

    return int(current)
